title: Directing Hole Utilization Through Self‐Reconstructed Crystallinity Differentiation for Photoelectrochemical Water Oxidation
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Photoelectrochemical water oxidation is limited not simply by light absorption, but by inefficient hole routing and utilization at the semiconductor‐electrolyte interface, together with severe defect‐mediated recombination. Here, a self‐reconstructed crystallinity‐differentiated interface is developed to program hole utilization in photoanodes. A one‐step hydrothermal synthesis creates an interlocked architecture in which highly crystalline In 2 S 3 pyramids are coupled with a disordered mixed‐anion nanosheet domain, generating a spatially polarized reaction field for directed hole accumulation and transfer. This reconstructed interface lowers the work function, redistributes the local coordination environment around In sites, and induces a spatially heterogeneous photovoltage landscape that promotes interfacial charge separation. Mild Ar annealing further serves as a defect‐selective activation step, suppressing recombination‐active defects while preserving the beneficial interfacial polarization, thereby accelerating charge injection and oxygen evolution kinetics. The optimized photoanode reaches 8.74 mA cm −2 at 1.23 V RHE , establishing interlocked crystallinity‐differentiated architecture engineering combined with defect‐selective activation as an effective strategy for sulfide photoanodes.

title: Electrochemically Driven Phenazine Autoxidation Coupled With Supported Liquid Membrane Technology for Hydrogen Peroxide Production
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Electrosynthesis offers a direct route to utilize clean electricity to create low–emission pathways for chemical manufacturing. For direct electrosynthesis of highly active compounds such as hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ), however, the close coupling of product formation and decomposition at electrode interfaces, together with energy intensive product–electrolyte separation, leads to energy losses and limited scalability. Here, we develop an electrified supported liquid membrane platform as a scalable and practical method for H 2 O 2 production as an important model compound. In this architecture, electrons from an external power source are temporarily stored in a designed organic mediator that is subsequently autoxidized within a physically segregated supported liquid membrane domain. This structural–decoupling strategy suppresses electrode driven decomposition, simplifies product handling, and permits independent tuning of electrochemical, transport, and product formation environments within a compact, modular device constructed from inexpensive components. The platform produces high–purity aqueous H 2 O 2 with Faradaic efficiencies up to 80%. We further demonstrate direct, on–site utilization of the generated oxidizing equivalents via in situ Fenton oxidation of an organic contaminant, thereby converting intermittent renewable electricity into localized water–treatment capability. More broadly, this strategy establishes an integrated and flexible reactor design framework for multiphase, electrochemically mediated synthetic processes beyond H 2 O 2 .

title: Reprogramming Stereocontrol Through Progressive Substrate Reorganization in Artificial Triplet Photoenzymes
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Precise control of stereoselectivity remains a fundamental challenge in artificial enzymatic catalysis, particularly for artificial photoenzymes that lack evolutionary coupling between photosensitizer positioning and substrate recognition. Herein, by integrating crystallography, kinetics, molecular simulations, and protein engineering, we show that the enantioselectivity of an artificial triplet photoenzyme TPe4.0_FBpA for [2+2] cycloaddition originates from a highly organized indole substrate assembly within the photoactive cavity. Guided by these insights, progressive remodeling of substrate organization through minimal active‐site engineering reverses enantiopreference (from 99.5:0.5 e.r. to 2:98 e.r.) while preserving the sequence position of the genetically encoded photosensitizer. Structural and computational analyses further support a switch in the dominant stereocontrol mode from template‐assisted substrate organization to dispersion‐driven conformational confinement. These findings establish substrate organization as a programmable determinant of stereochemical outcome in artificial photoenzymes and provide a mechanistic framework for stereodivergent excited‐state biocatalysis.

title: Lensless Wide‐Field Microscopy: Toward Next‐Generation Chemical Bioimaging
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Lensless imaging offers a new route to substantially alleviate the shackle of space‐bandwidth‐product (SBP) on conventional optical microscopes, thus high resolution and wide field‐of‐view (FOV) can be more easily achieved simultaneously. A series of lensless imaging methods have taken their place in chemical bioimaging due to their advantages of wide FOV and low cost. This review discusses the development of sensor‐proximal contact, incoherent, holographic, and ptychographic imaging and evaluates their applications across cellular phenotyping, particle and molecular sensing, as well as tissue and in vivo imaging. Particular emphasis is placed on interfacial chemical strategies involving affinity reagents, responsive materials, luminescent reactions, and engineered probes. These approaches convert nanoscale chemical events, which cannot be directly resolved by lensless systems, into amplified and spatially resolved optical signals. By combining chemical signal transduction with large‐area imaging, lensless platforms can detect individual cells, particles, and molecular events while simultaneously capturing their temporal dynamics, spatial organization, and collective evolution. This chemistry‐centered minireview highlights future opportunities for extracting multiscale spatiotemporal information from complex chemical and biological systems.

title: Topological Carbon Quantum Rings With Near‐Unity Photoluminescence for Efficient Sky‐Blue Electroluminescence
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Carbon quantum dots (CQDs) are promising environmentally benign emitters for next‐generation optoelectronic devices, yet aggregation‐caused quenching (ACQ) fundamentally limits their solid‐state emission efficiency. Existing strategies primarily rely on surface or morphological modifications, while the role of topology in regulating exciton behavior remains largely unexplored. Here, we report a topological design strategy to suppress ACQ by constructing carbon quantum rings with a closed‐loop conjugated architecture. Guided by symmetric molecular precursors, the ring formation process is elucidated by combined mass spectrometry and density functional theory (DFT) calculations, revealing a thermodynamically driven evolution from planar oligomers to curved and ultimately closed‐loop structures. This unique topology intrinsically suppresses intermolecular π–π coupling and non‐radiative decay, while enabling exciton confinement within a rigid conjugated framework. As a result, the carbon quantum rings exhibit a near‐unity photoluminescence quantum yield of 99.5% in solution and 58.9% in solid‐state films. When integrated into electroluminescent devices, efficient sky‐blue emission is achieved with a low turn‐on voltage of 2.8 V, a maximum luminance of 1020 cd m −2 , and an external quantum efficiency of 3.4%. This work establishes topology as a fundamental design parameter for carbon‐based emitters and provides a general strategy for overcoming ACQ in sustainable optoelectronic materials.

title: Design of Giant Negative Thermal Expansion Based on a Fluorite Structure
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Negative thermal expansion (NTE) is a unique phenomenon in which materials contract upon heating, and thus, there is a strong demand for rational synthetic strategies and the design of giant NTE materials. In tetracyanoborate salts, however, the formation of interpenetrated structures suppresses structural flexibility and limits NTE behavior. Herein, we demonstrated that constructing a fluorite structure is an effective strategy for enhancing NTE through the synthesis of Ba[B(CN) 4 ] 2 with toluene as a template molecule. Density functional theory calculations predicted that Ba[B(CN) 4 ] 2 exhibited pronounced volume contraction at elevated temperature among M[B(CN) 4 ] 2 (M = Ca 2+ , Sr 2+ , and Ba 2+ ). In situ X‐ray diffraction measurements showed that Ba[B(CN) 4 ] 2 exhibited giant NTE with a volumetric thermal expansion coefficient of α v = –122.0 × 10 −6 K −1 over 620–657 K after the removal of the template molecules. Phonon calculations revealed that giant NTE in Ba[B(CN) 4 ] 2 originates from a non‐rigid unit mode with strongly negative Grüneisen parameters. These findings provide a new design principle for synthesizing open‐framework materials with precisely controlled thermal expansion properties.

title: Photo‐Controlled Tandem Polymerization Enabled by a Dinuclear Salen‐Al Catalyst for Multiblock Copolymer Synthesis
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Expanding tandem polymerization beyond two mutually compatible cycles remains a formidable challenge, largely due to the stringent specificity required by most (photo)catalysts. Here, we report a dinuclear aluminum salen complex bridged by a trithiocarbonate linker that exhibits a unique intramolecular photoinduced energy/electron transfer (PET) process with fast kinetics. This catalyst enables a bidirectional chain propagation pathway and bridges vinyl monomers PET‐RAFT polymerization with epoxides/anhydrides ring‐opening copolymerization (ROCOP), racemic lactide ring‐opening polymerization (ROP), and step‐growth polymerization between in situ generated Al–O active species and diisocyanates. Under visible‐light regulation, PET‐RAFT polymerization exhibits selective on–off switching and can proceed concurrently or in tandem with ROCOP and ROP, whereas ROP occurs only after complete consumption of the anhydride in ROCOP. Leveraging the tandem nature of these four reactions under a single catalytic regime, we achieve the unprecedented one‐pot synthesis of (ABCBA) n multiblock copolymers. This approach establishes a versatile platform for constructing complex macromolecular architectures via multiple tandem polymerizations in a single reaction vessel.

title: Solvent‐Mediated Multi‐Factor Structural Modulation for Tunable Phosphorescence in Metal–Organic Frameworks
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Independently controlling phosphorescence dynamics while preserving the intrinsic emissive state is essential for establishing mechanistically clear framework‐phosphorescence relationships and rationally developing diverse phosphorescent metal–organic frameworks (MOFs). Yet conventional ligand/metal screening typically alters the emissive center. Herein, a novel solvent‐mediated multi‐factor structural modulation strategy yields five Zn‐based MOFs with tunable dimensionalities (1D, 2D, 3D) from a single metal/ligand system, exhibiting widely tunable phosphorescence lifetimes (12.6–1045.4 ms) and quantum yields (0.2%–16.2%), while retaining broadly similar ligand‐centered green emission, allowing kinetic differences to be attributed primarily to coupled structural variations. Single‐crystal structures reveal dimensional, terminal‐ligand, and guest‐confinement variations governing supramolecular interactions and framework rigidity. Theoretical analysis links these factors to distinct excited‐state localization, while γ/β descriptors link orbital mixing to intersystem crossing and radiative decay. Among the five structures, strong hydrogen bonding and guest confinement in the guest‐containing 2D MOF afford a 1045.4 ms lifetime, whereas semi‐chelate coordination and excited‐state localization in 1D MOF may favor a 16.2% quantum yield. These color‐stable, lifetime‐tunable materials enable covert exclusive‐OR optical encoding featuring parity‐check self‐validation and single‐bit error correction. This paradigm provides new chemical insights into decoupling phosphorescence dynamics from the intrinsic emissive state, enabling mechanistic elucidation and rational construction of multiscale, tailorable phosphorescent MOF systems.

title: Janus Nanoporous Metal–Phenolic Nanosheet Membranes for Highly Efficient Osmotic Energy Harvesting
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Osmotic energy, harvested by reverse electrodialysis, is a huge and promising renewable power source. However, the implementation still remains a longstanding bottleneck due to the lack of high‐efficiency membranes with both remarkable ionic conductivity and high permselectivity. Here, we report a new membrane constructed by Janus nanoporous metal–phenolic nanosheets (Janus MPNs), which overcomes the intrinsic trade‐off between ion permeability and selectivity. The Janus MPNs prepared via a facile interface‐induced coordination assembly strategy feature an asymmetric bilayer architecture comprising a microporous domain containing ∼0.96 nm pores and a mesoporous domain containing ∼9.4 nm pores, with each domain approximately 10 nm thick. The assembled Janus MPNs membrane integrates interlayer 2D nanofluidic pathways with ordered intralayer 1D nanochannels, enabling ultrafast ion transport rates approximately 21 times those of membranes relying solely on interlamellar transport. More importantly, the intrinsic sub‐nanometer pores and abundant negative surface charges within the metal–phenolic framework enable high cation selectivity, yielding a cation transference number ( t + ) of ∼0.936. When applied in reverse electrodialysis, the Janus MPNs membrane delivers a power density of 22.1 W m −2 under a simulated sea/river salinity gradient, outperforming state‐of‐the‐art two dimensional (2D)‐material‐based membranes. This work establishes new scaffolds for membrane technology and osmotic energy harvesting.

title: A Compact Fluorogenic Peptide Tag for Bright Wash‐Free Live‐Cell Imaging
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Live‐cell fluorescence imaging offers profound insights into cellular biology, yet achieving strong fluorescence signals with minimal labeling footprint and perturbation to proteins of interest remains a persistent challenge. Here we introduce FluoP‐tag, a compact fluorogenic peptide‐tag platform for tandem‐array engineering in live cells. FluoP‐tag combines a 31‐residue peptide (∼3.4 kDa) with a cell‐permeable fluorogenic dye, FluoP580 (568 Da), rationally engineered to undergo peptide‐triggered switching from a non‐emissive spirolactam state to an emissive zwitterionic state. This compact design enables wash‐free intracellular labeling and copy‐number‐dependent signal amplification in tandem‐array formats. An 8×FluoP array produced 3.37‐fold higher brightness than HaloTag labeled with a Rhodamine X‐derived probe while remaining smaller overall (∼29.5 kDa vs. ∼33 kDa). FluoP‐tag arrays further enabled protein imaging across diverse intracellular compartments, spanning biomolecular condensates in stress granules, the nucleus, and the nucleolus, and cytoskeletal architectures resolved by live‐cell structured illumination microscopy (SIM). FluoP‐tag provides a compact fluorogenic tag‐array platform for protein labeling and imaging in living cells.

title: Unraveling the Importance of Surface Hydrogen Diffusion in Photocatalysis by Isotope Probing
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Harnessing solar energy for hydrogen generation has motivated extensive efforts to optimize photocatalysts, yet reported efficiencies remain inadequate due to insufficient mechanistic understanding. Using a well‐defined Pt/TiO 2 (110) photocatalyst, time‐resolved mass spectrometry, and isotope probing, we show that surface hydrogen diffusion can constitute a key, yet largely overlooked, determinant of photocatalytic hydrogen evolution. Employing selected methanol isotopologues, we disentangle the roles of hydrogen atoms from different precursor positions in the reaction mechanism. We find that replacing 1 H with 2 H (D) suppresses the hydrogen evolution rate, resulting from kinetic limitations by deuterium migration across the oxide surface. For CD 3 OH, we show that deuterium is removed from the surface via hydroxy‐H/D exchange, drastically decreasing the D 2 formation and bypassing the diffusion bottleneck. Our findings establish hydrogen mobility as a critical component of hydrogen evolution and highlight control of surface transport processes as a promising route toward maximizing photocatalytic performance in hydrogen‐involving reactions.

title: Demonstration of a Two‐Electron Pathway in Piezoelectric Mechanochemistry: Synthesis and Mechanical Adaptation of Polythiourethane
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Mechanochemically initiated reactions have garnered interest as an unconventional method for generating new forms of reactivity. Previous studies have focused on radical‐mediated processes or two‐electron processes mediated by a ball‐milling mechanism. In this work, we present a novel mechano‐mediated reaction that utilizes focused ultrasound and mechanical vibration to generate both one‐electron and two‐electron thiol reactions in the same reaction pot. Interestingly, we find that the final reaction product can be biased depending on the reactive partner. We employ this newly reported two‐electron reaction to create the first vibrationally driven polythiourethane (PTU) through a two‐electron mechanism, as well as its adaptive polymer composites. This research presents an eco‐friendly, vibrationally promoted approach to polymer synthesis.

title: Lanthanide Separation via Selective Precipitation Under Neutral Aqueous Conditions With a Functionalized EDTA Chelator
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT In this study, we report a precipitation‐based strategy for recycling and refining neodymium (Nd) from permanent magnet e‐waste in neutral aqueous solution using a functionalized ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA) chelator. A hydrophobic substituent, carbostyril 124, was introduced onto the EDTA framework to yield EDTA‐cs124, which exhibited a solubility profile of the ensuing lanthanide complexes capable of differentiating the lighter and heavier lanthanides. The lighter lanthanide complexes precipitated markedly faster than the heavier ones, enabling efficient separation of Nd from a Nd/Dy/Tb mixture derived from waste hard disk drive (HDD) magnets. The recycled Nd could be refined by repeated precipitations to afford 99.3% Nd purity and 77% recovery yield. Using recyclable EDTA‐cs124 provides an operationally simple and organic‐solvent‐free approach for lanthanide separation.

title: An Alkali Amide Approach to Triphosphabenzenes
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT A new approach to triphosphabenzenes using simple and commercially available alkali amide reagents is presented. LiNMe 2 catalyzes the cyclotrimerization of triphenylmethylphosphaalkyne ( 1 ) and 1‐adamantylphosphaalkyne ( 3 ) to yield 2,4,6‐tris(triphenylmethyl)‐Dewar‐1,3,5‐triphosphabenzene ( 2 ) and 2,4,6‐tris(1‐adamantyl)‐1,3,5‐triphosphabenzene ( 4 ), respectively. The reaction is solvent dependent where non‐coordinating solvents allow the reaction to proceed catalytically. In contrast, tetrahydrofuran (THF) traps cyclic 1,3‐diphosphacyclobuten‐4‐yl ( 5 ) and λ 4 ‐triphosphabenzene anions ( 6 ) by intercepting the addition of LiNMe 2 during the cyclotrimerization of 1 . In the absence of the stabilizing effect of THF, LiNMe 2 is eliminated from 6 and the symmetric 1,3,5‐triphosphabenzene 2′ forms. By extending to other Group 1 amides, we show that KN(SiMe 3 ) 2 mediates the cyclotrimerization of 1 via a C( sp 3 )–H deprotonation of weakly acidic benzyl derivatives, allowing the synthesis and characterization of functionalized λ 4 ‐triphosphabenzene anions and λ 5 ‐triphosphabenzenes ( 9a to 9e ).

title: Unstable Oscillatory Modes Estimation in the Frequency Domain
abstract: Although frequency-domain analysis is a powerful tool for small-signal stability assessment in power systems, its sensitivity analyses generally aim at selected frequencies, particularly around poorly damped or undamped modes. However, reliably identifying the unstable frequencies within the frequency-domain framework remains a significant challenge. This work introduces and demonstrates a robust method based on the Generalized Nyquist Criterion for estimating unstable oscillatory frequencies, which overcomes the exposed limitations of existing techniques.

title: Uncertainty-Aware Robust Dynamic Operating Envelope for Safe Integration of Distributed Energy Resources
abstract: The increasing penetration of distributed energy resources (DERs) motivates the research on dynamic operating envelopes (DOEs), which are the power limits issued by utilities to DERs to ensure operational constraint compliance. However, the inherent load uncertainty and the non-convexity of power flow pose significant challenges to the optimization of DOEs. In this paper, a two-stage DOE optimization framework is proposed, where the first stage problem characterizes the optimal DOEs and the second stage problem checks the feasibility of DOE internal operating points against all possible uncertainty realizations. To ease computational burdens, a data-driven approach is leveraged to convexify the distribution power flow model for feasibility check. In this way, an efficient solution algorithm is proposed based on Benders decomposition, which converts the two-stage DOE optimization problem into two mixed-integer linear programming problems to be solved iteratively. Finally, through detailed case studies on the IEEE 123-node test feeder, the proposed method can achieve more robust and accurate DOEs than the benchmarks.

title: Quantum Depth-First Search-Based Reliability Assessment of Composite Generation and Transmission Systems
abstract: The acceleration of classical composite generation and transmission system reliability assessment is mainly achieved through algorithmic innovations at the state sampling stage. Typical approaches include combining machine learning techniques or scenario reduction methods with Monte Carlo simulation. The former improves computational efficiency at the expense of partial accuracy, while the latter relies on a large number of samples and thus reduces the effective number of reliability samples. In contrast, quantum computing possesses a theoretical speed advantage over classical computing owing to its unique superposition and entanglement properties, and it has been demonstrated to achieve quantum supremacy. Motivated by this potential, this paper proposes a composite generation and transmission system reliability assessment method based on quantum-inspired algorithms. First, a quantum depth-first search (DFS) algorithm considering path connectivity is developed to construct a quantum model of the initial node and transmission paths. This model remains invariant with respect to changes in system fault states and enables the direct identification of subsystems connected to the initial node. Second, a quantum-inspired reliability assessment framework for composite generation and transmission systems is proposed, in which a quantum depth-first search model and a quantum power flow calculation model are established. By alternately integrating quantum-inspired computation with classical computation, the reliability indices of the composite generation and transmission system can be efficiently evaluated. Finally, two designed test systems and the RBTS system are analyzed. The results demonstrate the effectiveness and correctness of the proposed quantum depth-first search algorithm and the quantum-inspired composite generation and transmission system reliability assessment model.

title: Cut-Selection Enhanced Risk-Averse Stochastic Dual Dynamic Programming for Economic Dispatch With Carbon Capture Systems
abstract: This paper investigates a multi-stage stochastic economic dispatch problem for power systems with carbon capture systems (MCCSED). The focus is on effectively managing operational risks through a risk-averse approach. To efficiently solve this challenging problem, a cut-selection-enhanced risk-averse stochastic dual dynamic programming (SDDP) algorithm is developed, incorporating an enhanced test of usefulness (ETOU) strategy to remedy the premature discarding of valid cuts inherent in the conventional level 1 (L1) method. Case studies on IEEE 39-bus, 118-bus, and 300-bus systems yield these findings. First, higher carbon capture installation rates enhance risk management through increased storage flexibility. Second, the risk-averse approach reduces tail-risk costs and enables more intuitive parameter tuning than distributionally robust optimization, revealing a consistent two-phase pattern across risk management approaches and underscoring the importance of coordinating risk management and flexibility. Third, the proposed ETOU-L1 method offers competitive convergence by recovering valid cuts usually discarded by the conventional L1 method, while demonstrating scalability for large-scale problems.

title: Integrated Bayesian Inference for Online Inertia Estimation With Non Gaussian Posterior in Inverter Based Resources Interfaced Power Systems
abstract: In modern low inertia power systems with high inverter penetration, online inertia estimation has become challenging due to the presence of nonlinear converter control, virtual inertia loops, current saturation, measurement errors, and other practical uncertainties. To overcome these challenges, this paper presents an advanced Tree Pyramidal Adaptive Importance Sampling based Bayesian inference approach for the estimation of inertia and virtual inertia in an inverter-interfaced power system. Since the proposed algorithm possesses an adaptive proposal distribution refinement, it effectively explores the most probable parameter space. Hence, it reduces variance in inertia estimation results and converges early to the desired value of the inertia constant with fewer samples. The sample generation process is fully parallel, which supports faster execution. The proposed algorithm is robust against non-Gaussian posteriors that may arise due to non-linearity in the inertia estimation problem. The algorithm is hyperparameter-tuning-free and possesses an anytime property. The proposed algorithm is tested for inertia estimation in an IEEE 9 bus system interfaced with a PV-battery grid-following inverter for different scenarios of load shedding, load increment, weak and strong grids, non-Gaussian posterior, and Gaussian noise. Simulation and real-time results validate the superior performance of the proposed method for inertia estimation.

title: Approximating Dispatchable Regions in Three-Phase Radial Networks With Conditions for Exact SDP Relaxation
abstract: The concept of dispatchable region plays a pivotal role in quantifying the capacity of power systems to accommodate renewable generation. In this paper, we extend the previous approximations of the dispatchable regions based on direct current (DC), linearized, and nonlinear single-phase alternating current (AC) models to unbalanced three-phase radial (tree) networks and provide improved outer and inner approximations of dispatchable regions. Based on the nonlinear bus injection model (BIM), we relax the non-convex problem that defines the dispatchable region to a solvable semidefinite program (SDP) and derive its strong dual problem (which is also an SDP). Utilizing the special mathematical structure of the dual problem, an SDP-based projection algorithm is developed to construct a convex polytopic outer approximation to the SDP-relaxed dispatchable region. Moreover, we provide sufficient conditions to guarantee the exact SDP relaxation by adding the power loss as a penalty term, thereby providing a theoretical guarantee for determining an inner approximation of the dispatchable region. Through numerical simulations, we validate the accuracy of our approximation of the dispatchable region and verify the conditions for exact SDP relaxation.

title: Analytical Framework for Assessing Effective Regional Inertia
abstract: This paper proposes a novel formulation of effective regional inertia that explicitly accounts for both system topology and the spatial distribution of inertia. Unlike traditional approaches that model a region as an aggregated machine with an equivalent inertia, the proposed metric provides a topology-aware representation. The methodology builds on an analytical framework that extends classical slow coherency theory to address network partitioning and regional frequency stability. Based on these partitions, we develop a systematic procedure to evaluate the effective inertia of each region, enabling a more accurate interpretation of local inertial contributions, including those from virtual inertia provided by inverter-based resources (IBRs). Case studies on the IEEE 39-bus, 68-bus, and a reduced version of the Brazilian Interconnected system demonstrate that the integration of inertial devices does not uniformly improve system frequency response, underscoring the importance of the proposed metric for effective regional inertia assessment.

title: Interpolatory Approximations of PMU Data: Dimension Reduction and Pilot Selection
abstract: This work investigates the reduction of phasor measurement unit (PMU) data through low-rank matrix approximations. To reconstruct a PMU data matrix from fewer measurements, we propose the framework of interpolatory matrix decompositions (IDs). In contrast to methods relying on principal component analysis or singular value decomposition, IDs recover the complete data matrix using only a few of its rows (PMU datastreams) and/or a few of its columns (snapshots in time). This row-/column-based compression enables real-time monitoring of power transmission systems using measurements from a smaller subset of pilot datastreams, thereby minimizing communication bandwidth. The ID perspective gives a rigorous error bound on the quality of the data compression. We propose selecting the pilot measurements used in an ID via the discrete empirical interpolation method (DEIM), a greedy algorithm that aims to control the error bound. This bound yields a computable estimate of the reconstruction error during online operations. A violation of this estimate suggests a change in the system’s operating conditions and thus serves as a tool for fault detection. Following a disturbance, DEIM can be used to localize the event source across all buses with high accuracy. Numerical tests on synthetic PMU data demonstrate DEIM’s excellent performance in data compression and validate the proposed DEIM-based fault-detection and localization method.

title: A Pseudo-Transient-Enhanced Trajectory-Unified Method for Deterministically Computing Multiple ACOPF Solutions: Methods and Computation
abstract: The feasible region of Alternating Current Optimal Power Flow (ACOPF) models often comprises multiple disjoint feasible components. Each feasible component may contain one or more local optimal solutions (LOSs). Conventional ACOPF solution methodologies typically compute only a single OPF solution and may thereby overlook potential high-value alternative OPF solutions. This paper presents a deterministic numerical method, PGS-TT, to systematically compute all LOSs within each feasible component. PGS-TT integrates the Projected Gradient System with the Trust-Tech framework. This deterministic four-stage method consists of: 1) converging to an LOS; 2) escaping from the current LOS and moving toward another possible OPF solution; 3) detecting the existence of another LOS; and 4) computing the newly detected OPF solution. The proposed numerical PGS-TT method is enhanced by several novel numerical schemes designed to ensure computational efficiency and scalability for large-scale ACOPF models. The method’s effectiveness is demonstrated on several modified IEEE test systems: 118-bus, 500-bus, 1,888-bus, and 30,000-bus. Notably, numerical studies reveal several OPF cases where the higher-cost OPF solution exceeds the lower-cost one by up to 51.45%, highlighting the critical need to compute multiple high-quality LOSs to improve the security and economic efficiency of power system operation and planning.

title: 2026 Index IEEE Transactions on Power Systems
AutoHPFL: Autonomous Physics-Data Hybrid Power Flow Linearization Design via LLM Agents
abstract: This letter presents AutoHPFL, an autonomous algorithm-design framework that coordinates large language model (LLM) agents to explore and refine Physics-data-hybrid-driven power flow linearization (HPFL) methods. Rather than relying on manually crafted feature mappings, AutoHPFL autonomously searches the design space of linearization strategies through structured exploration, where agents iteratively refine candidates via tree-informed reflection on real-environment execution feedback, coordinated through novelty-aware Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) to systematically identify high-performing methods beyond manual feature engineering. Experiments on IEEE 118-bus, 300-bus and 33-bus test systems demonstrate up to 35.9% error reduction over representative baselines. Moreover, the generated candidates exhibit interpretable design patterns, such as physics-guided feature construction and topology-aware local modeling, indicating the potential of LLM-agent search for autonomous power system algorithm design.

title: Generalized Passivity Sensitivity Methodology for Small-Signal Stability Analysis in Converter-Dominated Power Systems
abstract: This paper proposes a generalized passivity sensitivity analysis for power system small-signal stability. The method quantifies the impact of device parameters and subsystems on the passivity index at both the device and system levels. Explicit sensitivity expressions are derived by exploiting the particular structures of the admittance and nodal models. The proposed analysis identifies the dominant contributors to non-dissipative behavior, thereby enabling effective passivation strategies. These proposed analyses, based on the developed sensitivities, are validated across different parameters at the device and system levels. In addition, we demonstrate how to utilize the proposed method through case studies with different converter controls, showing its general applicability.

title: Cycle-Aware Adaptive Mixture-of-Experts With High-Demand-Sensitive Asymmetric Loss for Effective Electrical Load Forecasting
abstract: Accurate load forecasting is critical for reliable and economical power system operation, particularly during high-demand periods. However, increasing demand volatility and distributed energy integration pose substantial challenges to forecasting rare but impactful high-demand periods. While deep learning has improved general forecasting capabilities, existing models often struggle to accurately predict rapid load surges during high-demand scenarios. To address this issue, we propose an Cycle-Aware Adaptive Mixture-of-Experts (CAMoE) model that simultaneously enhances overall forecasting accuracy and sensitivity to high-demand scenarios. CAMoE consists of three modules: the Cycle-Aware Residual Learning Module (CaRLM) explicitly decouples load sequences into periodic, trend, and fluctuation components; the Context-Adaptive Mixture-of-Experts (ConMoE) employs dynamic routing to activate specialized experts based on demand characteristics; and the Hierarchical Temporal Fusion Module (HTFM) integrates feature representations across different temporal components to generate the final predictions. To further improve performance under high-demand conditions, CAMoE is trained with a High-Demand-Sensitive Asymmetric (DeSA) loss, which penalizes underestimation during peak periods while maintaining training stability. Extensive experiments on real-world datasets demonstrate that CAMoE reduces MAE and RMSE by a maximum of 10.64% and 10.00% compared to the second-best baseline under high-demand scenarios. Additionally, DeSA exhibits strong generalizability across various forecasting models, demonstrating its practical value in modern power systems.

title: A Fast Convergent Distribution Power Flow for Systems With P-$|$V$|$ Nodes
abstract: This paper proposes a fast convergent power flow technique for power distribution systems with P-<inline-formula><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$|$</tex-math></inline-formula>V<inline-formula><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$|$</tex-math></inline-formula> controlled distributed energy resources (DERs). The proposed power flow algorithm enhances Iwamoto’s method to accommodate the multi-phase distribution power flow equations and includes distribution-specific ZIP (polynomial) injection models. Proofs of convergence are shown for both the original and proposed algorithms. The convergent behavior of the new method with P-<inline-formula><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$|$</tex-math></inline-formula>V<inline-formula><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$|$</tex-math></inline-formula> controlled DER and ZIP load models is illustrated using the IEEE 13-Bus Feeder and two larger, actual distribution circuits. Convergence analysis of the proposed method and other solvers is performed for different system operating conditions. Computational runtime analysis also demonstrates the proposed method’s speed advantage over other solvers.

title: Decentralized Analytic Bayesian Probabilistic Composite Load Modeling: Sensitivity, Identifiability and Interpretability
abstract: With the widespread deployment of phasor measurement units (PMUs), data-driven composite load modeling has gained increasing attention among researchers. Existing approaches mainly rely on optimization-based methods to produce point estimates, which lack the capability to quantify estimation uncertainty. Alternatively, sampling-based techniques can provide confidence intervals (CIs) but are computationally expensive for real-time applications. In addition, the theoretical interpretability of such CIs is still limited. To address these issues, we propose a decentralized Bayesian load modeling strategy utilizing trajectory sensitivity that achieves structural decoupling between the load model and the external network. It eliminates the effects associated with external uncertainties in the system while effectively providing a probabilistic description of the load parameters, without resorting to time-consuming sampling. Moreover, for the first time we derive an analytical relation between trajectory sensitivities, measurement Jacobians, priors, noise, and confidence levels, theoretically demonstrating the rationale of key parameter screening in a statistical manner. The simulation results for multiple load modeling cases reveal the excellent performance of the proposed method.

title: Identification and Enhancement of Transient Voltage Oscillation Stability Involved With Switching Dynamic Process
abstract: Due to the nonlinear switching dynamics of inverter-based resources (IBRs, repeated low-voltage ride-through (LVRT) behavior has induced transient voltage oscillation phenomena, which have emerged in recent years, posing a substantial threat to the security and stability of modern power systems. To address this issue, this paper proposes a transient voltage instability identification method and coordinated control strategy for renewable energy systems. Firstly, a hybrid differential-algebraic equation (DAE) system model incorporating sequential switching dynamics of IBRs is established. Subsequently, the dynamic response trajectories of the system corresponding to voltage instability phenomenon are accurately characterized through voltage bifurcation manifold theory, and a transient voltage instability identification method is proposed. Moreover, the impacts of dominant parameters on the switching process and transient voltage oscillation severity are analyzed. Finally, a multi-level coordinated control strategy is proposed based on the transient voltage instability criterion, and simulations conducted on real renewable energy station systems verify the effectiveness of the transient voltage instability identification method and the coordinated control strategy.

title: Proactive Resilient UC Against Typhoon-Induced Cascading Failures via a Data-Driven Surrogate
abstract: Extreme weather-driven cascading failures (CFs) in power systems can lead to catastrophic socioeconomic losses, yet integrating CF analysis directly into day-ahead proactive unit commitment (UC) is mathematically intractable. This difficulty arises from representing decision-dependent topology evolution within a tractable UC formulation. To address this challenge, a resilient UC framework is proposed, featuring a data-driven surrogate that encodes CF risks into a tractable polyhedral region. First, overload-induced CF simulations are performed offline across diverse commitment and dispatch states under contingencies. To capture nonlinear CF boundaries in the system's discrete-continuous operating space, a sequential training strategy is employed to construct a surrogate consisting of a series of linear classifiers. This surrogate identifies a polyhedral region with low CF risk, which can be directly integrated into the UC model as linear constraints for CF-aware decision-making. Case studies show that the proposed strategy significantly reduces the expected loss of load by proactively mitigating CF risks with only a marginal increase in operating costs, offering a streamlined yet effective pathway for enhancing power system resilience.

title: Modeling, Analysis, and Control of Active Distribution Networks With Smart Loads
abstract: Electric spring (ES) has been introduced as a fast demand response (DR) technology that can vary the power consumption of its associated noncritical load (NCL) for bus voltage support and frequency stabilization. The combined use of ES and NCL creates a new generation of smart load (SL) technology. Furthermore, the connection of many SLs forms a smart load network (SLN), which can perform coordinated grid support functions. To further understand the usefulness of SLN, this paper provides a comprehensive investigation of the modeling and analysis of SLN in distribution grids. The detailed state-space model of the SL unit is investigated, which covers the average model of the inverter circuit, outer bus voltage loop, and inner voltage loop. Based on this state-space model, a new method of calculating the power flow of an arbitrary SLN is elaborated. The method relies on the establishment of three coefficient matrices to form a system of linear equations, which is done by simply observing the physical topology of an SLN. By solving the equations, the real-time bus voltage and SL power can be readily obtained. The integration of the state-space model of SL agents and the SLN model creates a simple and powerful tool to study the performance of the SLN in providing voltage regulation, assisting further research in the control of the active distribution network (ADN). Case studies demonstrate the usefulness of the proposed SLN model in providing voltage regulation and low-voltage ride-through (LVRT) support.

title: Threshold-Free Full-Process Monitoring of Power System Oscillation Based on Data-Structure Feature Fusion
abstract: The increasing penetration of renewable energy and extensive use of power electronic devices have made oscillations more prevalent in power systems. Accurate identification and tracking of oscillation evolution are essential for early warning and source tracing. However, precisely characterizing and recognizing these oscillations in real time is highly challenging due to their nonlinear, nonstationary, and multi-time-scale nature. This paper presents a full-process adaptive approach for oscillation monitoring based on data-structure feature fusion. Firstly, the intrinsic localized mode (ILM) theory is employed to qualitatively analyze the three-stage evolution of oscillation. Next, the ensemble empirical mode decomposition (EEMD) and variance contribution rate (VCR) criterion are applied to extract the dominant intrinsic mode function (IMF) components. From these components, Gramian angular summation field (GASF) phase maps and Hilbert-Huang spectrum (HHS) time-frequency maps are subsequently constructed to represent the structural features of the data. A Swin-Cross Attention Transformer (S-CAT) network is further designed to fuse heterogeneous image features and classify evolution patterns, and a decision strategy is introduced for full-process monitoring. Experimental tests show that the method achieves high recognition accuracy and offers early warning during the initial disturbance stage, demonstrating strong engineering applicability.

title: Development of an Application-Directed Distribution Network Equivalent for Transmission Planning Studies
abstract: Transmission planners require simple, transparent active distribution network equivalents (ADNEs) to accurately model distribution feeders with high penetration of converter-interfaced resources. Existing ADNE approaches rely on complex algorithms, hindering their routine adoption in transmission (bulk power system) planning studies; furthermore, validation has been confined to synthetic test networks. Thus, this letter presents an application-oriented procedure that reduces a detailed distribution feeder to a three-phase three-segment (TPTS) equivalent while preserving the original feeder characteristics required for transmission planning studies. The proposed approach has been validated on a real-world feeder in Arizona, modeled in DIgSILENT PowerFactory.

title: Physics-Shielded Deep Reinforcement Learning for Adaptive Emergency Frequency Control
abstract: The increasing penetration of renewable energy technologies is making power system frequency behaviour more complex. This evolving landscape challenges the reliability of conventional frequency control methods in maintaining system security, particularly the Under-Frequency Load Shedding (UFLS) scheme. Specifically, UFLS relies on predefined fixed thresholds and assumes stable patterns of generation and demand. These assumptions no longer hold in today's systems with variable renewables, changing demand, and bidirectional power flows. Although Adaptive UFLS (AUFLS) schemes have emerged, many rely on physics-agnostic Reinforcement Learning (RL), leading to inefficient training, high computational requirements—making scalability in large networks challenging—and suboptimal convergence. To address this, we propose a Physics-Shielded Deep RL (PS-DRL) method. Based on the Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) algorithm, the framework embeds physics-inspired constraints through a “Physics Shield” and uses real-time detection of system coherence to identify locational frequency characteristics, reducing unnecessary sampling and improving training efficiency. Validation results on the modified IEEE 39-bus and Texas 2000-bus systems demonstrate that PS-DRL converges up to 35% faster and reduces load shedding by 70% compared to existing RL approaches, while also showing good scalability.

title: Accelerating Power Flow Calculation in Hybrid AC/DC Distribution Networks via Decomposition of Partial Control Parameters and State Variables
abstract: To facilitate efficient and robust power flow (PF) analysis in multi-voltage-level hybrid AC/DC distribution networks (HAD-DNs), this letter proposes an accelerated computational method through decomposition of partial control parameters of dual active bridge (DAB) converters and system state variables. First, a comprehensive PF model incorporating voltage source converters (VSCs) and DAB converters is established, explicitly considering their distinct control modes. Then, an optimization approach for DAB control variables based on the Karush–Kuhn–Tucker (KKT) conditions is introduced, along with a unified iterative method to simultaneously determine system state variables and VSC control parameters. Case studies on HAD-DNs of different scales demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method and its improved convergence performance compared with conventional methods.

title: SFF-GAN: A Statistical Feature-Feedback GAN for AI-Driven Fault Diagnosis in IBR-Dominated Microgrids
Frequency-Domain Characterization of Load Demand From Electrified Highways
abstract: Electrified roadways (ER) equipped with dynamic wireless power transfer (DWPT) capabilities can patently extend the driving range and reduce the battery size of electric vehicles (EVs). However, due to the spatial arrangement of the transmitter coils in the ER, the DWPT load exhibits frequency content that could excite power system frequency dynamics. In this context, this work aims to study the spectrum of DWPT loads under different traffic conditions. Under simplifying assumptions, we develop statistical models to identify the location and relative magnitude of DWPT load harmonics. Our analysis reveals that the fundamental frequency depends on ER coil spacing and average EV speed. In the worst-case yet unlikely scenario that EVs move in a synchronized fashion, the amplitude of harmonics scales with the EV count. On the contrary, when EVs move freely, harmonics scale with the square root of the EV count. Platoon formations can accentuate harmonics. The spectral content around harmonics decreases in magnitude and increases in bandwidth with the harmonic index. The load of a single EV moving at a time-varying speed can be modeled as a frequency-modulated (FM) signal. Despite the simplifying assumptions, the derived models offer valuable insights for ER planners and grid operators. Dynamic simulations of a modified WECC model with DWPT loads synthesized from realistic EV trajectories and ER specifications corroborate some of these insights.

title: A Data-Driven Physics-Informed Defense Framework of DC Microgrids Against Cyberattacks
abstract: The increasing prevalence of DC microgrids (DCmGs) has exposed them to severe cybersecurity challenges, particularly false data injection (FDI) and denial-of-service (DoS) attacks. To address these threats, this paper proposes a data-driven physics-informed defense framework that efficiently integrates precise attack detection with smooth system recovery. At its core lies a physics-informed temporal generative adversarial network architecture (PiGAN). This model innovatively incorporates a linear attention mechanism to enhance temporal feature extraction. Simultaneously, it introduces physical constraints to ensure the reconstructed data strictly adhere to the intrinsic physical laws of DCmGs. To achieve accurate detection, an agent-based dynamic threshold detector is designed. This detector allows the system to adjust its anomaly sensitivity based on real-time operating conditions, thereby identifying dynamic and subtle attacks with high precision. Furthermore, to maintain system stability, a confidence-based smooth recovery strategy is developed. This strategy performs a dynamic weighted fusion of measured and reconstructed healthy data to enable a seamless transition from the attacked state to normal operation. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves an attack detection accuracy of up to 99.49%, effectively mitigating various malicious attacks and validating the framework’s efficiency and robustness.

title: Resilience Equity-Aware Distribution System and Energy Community Co-Planning With a Fair Subsidy Allocation Mechanism
abstract: Energy communities (ECs) are emerging as key actors in enhancing distribution system (DS) resilience. As the DS and multiple ECs participate in local planning and investment, a major challenge arises: how to coordinate their actions to ensure efficient and equitable access to resilience-enhancing resources across the system. To address this issue, this paper proposes a cooperative game-theoretic framework for joint resilience-enhancing planning of the DS with multiple ECs. The DS operator conducts grid expansion to facilitate the integration of distributed renewable energy sources (RESs). Concurrently, multiple ECs develop their distributed RES portfolios, optimizing for self-sufficiency while managing operational profitability uncertainties. Furthermore, resilience equity is defined as ensuring that all communities have equitable access to resilience services. Subsidies for distributed RES investment are allocated to ECs directly tied to their contribution to system resilience, with resilience equity serving as a fundamental factor in this assessment. Additionally, as exact Shapley value computation becomes intractable in large-scale systems, a stratified sampling approach is developed to achieve efficient and accurate approximations. Simulation studies on a modified European low-voltage test feeder demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in enhancing resilience while promoting resilience equity.

title: Grid-Aware Islanding and Resynchronisation of AC/DC Microgrids
abstract: This paper proposes an optimal, grid-aware supervisory control framework for the islanding, islanded operation, and resynchronisation of hybrid AC/DC microgrids. The framework relies on a unified hybrid AC/DC power flow (PF) model that explicitly represents the grid-forming operation of AC/DC interfacing converters (ICs). Sensitivity coefficients (SCs) are derived from this model and used to formulate the voltage and branch-current constraints of the optimal power flow (OPF). The considered operating mode is relevant for hybrid microgrids that aggregate DC-native or DC-interfaced resources, such as photovoltaic units, batteries, and electric vehicles, through a DC network. During islanded operation, the grid-forming IC regulates the AC voltage and frequency, while the active-power balance is supplied through the DC grid. This separates the active- and reactive-power slack locations and requires a dedicated PF and SC formulation. The proposed OPF computes the optimal setpoints that satisfy voltage and ampacity constraints before, during, and after the islanding manoeuvre, while local converter controls ensure voltage and frequency regulation in real time. The proposed framework is experimentally validated on a 27-node hybrid AC/DC network with three ICs and a mix of controllable and stochastic resources.

title: Model Predictive Black Start for Dynamic Formation of DER-Led Microgrids With Inrush Current Impacts
abstract: Black start (BS) of the distribution system (DS) with high penetration of distributed energy resources (DERs) requires advanced control frameworks to ensure secure and efficient restoration. This paper proposes a model predictive black start (MPBS) framework that captures the mutual interaction between switching decisions and physical feasibility to generate restoration sequences. Short-term forecasts of DER output, load demand, and transmission grid (TG) availability are incorporated within a receding-horizon control structure to construct cranking paths. To evaluate decision-dependent feasibility, an analytical inrush current estimation method is developed based on dynamically formed microgrid (MG) nodal impedance matrices under worst-case (WC) switching conditions. To mitigate excessive inrush current and prevent protection misoperations, a structural preventive mechanism is introduced, combining an emergency operation–inspired voltage reduction strategy with a switch-blocking function executed in a hierarchical manner. The proposed inrush model is validated against electromagnetic transient (EMT) simulations in PowerFactory with estimation accuracies exceeding 90%. Case studies on IEEE and EPRI networks demonstrate that the proposed MPBS framework effectively prevents fuse and recloser misoperations, reduces DER energy consumption, and improves load restoration efficiency during DER-led BS processes.

title: Vulnerability Analysis of Multi-Timescale DC Microgrids Under False Data Injection Attacks
abstract: This paper presents a vulnerability analysis for the multi-timescale DC microgrid (DCmG) against false data injection (FDI) attacks. Using singular perturbation theory, the system dynamics are decomposed into a fast boundary layer subsystem and a slow reduced-order model. Sufficient stability conditions for both subsystems are derived, and input-to-state stability (ISS) of the slow subsystem is established under attacks. Furthermore, a zonotopic reachability analysis is performed to estimate the worst-case state deviation and compute an analytical admissible attack indicator for safety assessment. Theoretical predictions are validated through both numerical simulations and full-hardware experiments. It is demonstrated that the multi-timescale property leads to new attack surfaces, and the analytical attack bounds are consistent with observed voltage deviations, which can effectively guide safe and secure control under cyber threats.

title: Adaptive Inertia of DC-Link Voltage Synchronization
abstract: DC-link voltage synchronization (DCVS) can be the virtual synchronous generator (VSG) strategy for grid-forming converter, but its virtual inertia configuration problem remains unsolved. Therefore, this paper proposes a universal adaptive virtual inertia strategy for DCVS. The desired virtual inertia adaptively decreases with the rise of DC-link voltage deviation (frequency deviation), which is entirely opposite to that of the traditional VSG ignoring DC-link voltage dynamic. To configure the desired adaptive virtual inertia, the AC frequency of the interfaced inverter is correlated with the energy stored in DC-link capacitor by the linear proportional and power-law logic. It can effectively alleviate the trade-off problem between DC-link voltage fluctuation and power angle overshoot under large power variation for better dynamic performance. Moreover, it can improve the dynamic performance (less DC-link voltage fluctuation) not in the cost of the steady-state performance (low-frequency-resonance suppressing capability) by not increasing the loop gain around the equilibrium point. The real-time simulation based on NI-PXI and power hardware-in-the-loop (PHIL) experiment validate its effectiveness and advantages compared to traditional methodology.

title: Distribution Operating Security Space-Based Power Decoupling Mechanism of Multiple Virtual Power Plants
abstract: The power-flow constraints introduce strong power coupling of multiple virtual power plants (VPPs) in a distribution system, thereby increasing computational complexity and causing interdependent decision-making among VPPs. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a distribution operating security space (DOSS) based power decoupling mechanism of multiple VPPs. Independence, fairness, and customization are developed to characterize DOSS. First, a novel dual super-ellipsoid security region is constructed as a convex inner approximation of the power-flow space, ensuring distribution grid security while enabling customized DOSS formation. Second, the matrix decomposition, parametric programming, and constraint reasoning are employed to convert the DOSS's property descriptions into an optimization formulation. The convex quadratic DOSS derived from the optimization can be efficiently embedded into the aggregation and disaggregation of VPPs. It can satisfy the requirements of grid operational security and diversified independent operation of VPPs. Case studies show that the power transfers among multiple VPPs are effectively decoupled, and DOSS is equitably allocated in a differentiated scheme. Compared with other methods, the aggregated capacity of VPPs is significantly higher, and no power-flow violations occur during VPP operation.

title: V2G Coordination for Secure and Low-Carbon Operation of EV-Rich Distribution Systems: A Safe Reinforcement Learning Approach
abstract: The increasing popularization of electric vehicles (EVs) offers opportunities to reduce carbon emissions via vehicle-to-grid (V2G) coordination. This paper proposes a secure and low-carbon V2G coordination framework for EV fleets based on the proposed grid-interactive multi-region model (GMM), which characterizes realistic EV operation patterns (e.g., charging, discharging, and driving) impacted by complex V2G coordination and enables accurate impact analysis of EV aggregation on the EV-rich distribution system (ERDS). To effectively learn a secure V2G coordination policy in ERDS with infrequent voltage violation signals, a bounded PID (BPID) Lagrangian safe reinforcement learning (BPID-SRL) method is proposed, aiming to optimize carbon emissions without inducing voltage violations. A Transformer-GNN (TG) agent is then designed to jointly handle the spatiotemporal complexity of V2G coordination in ERDS, thereby enhancing the performance of the proposed BPID-SRL. A case study based on a modified IEEE 33-bus system empirically demonstrates the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed BPID-SRL and its big potential to exploit V2G coordination for secure and low-carbon operations of ERDS.

title: Fairness and Voltage-Quality Enhancement Through Active–Reactive Dynamic Operating Envelopes in Unbalanced Low-Voltage Networks
abstract: This paper presents a novel fairness-aware dynamic operating envelope (DOE) framework for equitable active and reactive power allocations in unbalanced low-voltage (LV) networks with high penetration of distributed energy resources (DERs). The proposed method extends proportional fairness from conventional active power definitions to apparent power, allowing customers constrained in active export to contribute via reactive power support. A multi-phase current–voltage optimal power flow (OPF) formulation is developed, incorporating inverter capability constraints, transformer loading limits, and voltage unbalance factor (VUF) mitigation. The VUF is explicitly regularised to address phase-level voltage quality issues arising from asymmetric DER installations and single-phase connections. Time-series simulations on a real-world Australian LV feeder demonstrate that the proposed Fair $(P,Q)$ DOE with explicit VUF regularisation consistently maintains transformer and voltage constraints, reduces VUF below industry guidelines, and improves both fairness and network utilisation compared to existing methods. Results confirm that integrating reactive power flexibility and unbalance-aware fairness metrics enables a more inclusive and power-quality-compliant operation of DER-rich LV networks.

title: Distribution-Level Local Imbalance Market for Multi-Timescale Settlement and Network-Constrained Balancing
abstract: Existing local energy markets (LEMs) and local flexibility markets (LFMs) in distribution systems are primarily designed to facilitate energy trading and alleviate congestion. However, they lack explicit mechanisms for modeling nodal power deviations, pricing marginal imbalance costs, and allocating fast frequency response. This paper proposes a local imbalance market (LIM) that introduces a node-level imbalance formulation and distribution locational imbalance prices (DLIPs), internalizing network constraints and the balancing costs induced by power imbalances. The LIM incorporates a multi-timescale clearing structure where the distribution system operator (DSO) computes minute-level balancing decisions and DLIPs. A frequency response sensitivity matrix (FRSM) allocates second-scale fast-response costs to the nodes that caused the deviations. A native ADMM-based LIM clearing algorithm is designed to achieve scalable, privacy-preserving coordination among prosumers, aggregators, and the DSO without revealing private information. The second-scale allocation algorithm ensures cost causality and budget consistency through real-time measurement and ex-post reconciliation. Case studies on three modified distribution networks demonstrate that the proposed LIM enhances balancing efficiency, preserves participant privacy, and achieves accurate cost attribution under renewable uncertainty. The LIM provides a practical and economically consistent pathway for integrating renewable-rich resources into distribution-level market operations.

title: Federated Heterogeneous-Agent Reinforcement Learning for the Flexible Dispatch of Energy Hubs
abstract: Energy hubs (EHs) are important district multi-energy systems that integrate various carriers for energy conversion and storage. For the flexible dispatch of EHs, reinforcement learning (RL) has been a promising solution, capable of effectively and efficiently handling inherent uncertainties within EHs. However, the sample inefficiency issue of RL could lead to computational burden and suboptimal policies. More recently, federated reinforcement learning (FRL) has emerged as a new paradigm that improves sample efficiency by coordinating the learning processes of multiple agents. In this work, we introduce FRL for flexible dispatch of EHs and, specifically, propose a federated heterogeneous-agent reinforcement learning (FHRL) framework to overcome the challenges posed by inter-agent heterogeneity, which could lead to training instability and performance degradation in FRL. Our framework features an adaptive model aggregation method that extracts generalized knowledge of dispatch policies to generate the global model. Furthermore, it incorporates a knowledge transfer mechanism that leverages the generalized knowledge to guide the optimization of each local policy. Extensive experiments confirm our framework outperforms traditional RL and FRL in dispatch costs while demonstrating scalability in a large-scale scenario involving 50 heterogeneous EHs.

title: An Exact Discrete Aggregation Model to Cluster Identical Distributed Energy Resources With Discrete Operational Behaviors in Virtual Power Plants
Power Oscillation Mitigation of Inverter-Interfaced Distributed Energy Resources in Microgrids Under Unbalanced Faults
abstract: Three-phase four-wire Inverter-Interfaced Distributed Energy Resources (3P4W-DERs) offer significant advantages, including reduced emissions, localized energy production, and enhanced reliability for modern power systems. However, during unbalanced fault conditions, 3P4W-DERs may generate oscillatory active and reactive power components. These oscillations lead to DC-link fluctuations, overcurrent stress on power electronic devices, and potential system instabilities. To mitigate these issues, this paper proposes a Triple Current Controller (TCC) based on positive-, negative-, and zero-sequence components. The TCC is designed to eliminate instantaneous power oscillations while ensuring the generated current remains within safe operating limits, even under severe unbalanced fault conditions. The proposed method eliminates the need for complex sequence extraction techniques, thereby reducing control complexity. Also, a current limiting strategy is integrated into the controller to enforce peak current constraints during fault events. The proposed TCC is adaptive to both grid-connected and islanded modes of microgrid operation. Simulation results confirm the TCC’s ability to suppress active and reactive power oscillations without exceeding current limits under a wide range of unbalanced fault scenarios.

title: Correlation-Exploiting False Data Injection Attack and Corresponding DRL-Based Detection Countermeasure in Partially Observable Grids
abstract: In partially observable power grids, limited knowledge of grid topology and correlated nodal injections presents significant challenges to cybersecurity, complicating the development of stealthy false data injection attacks (FDIAs). To address these issues, this paper proposes an optimization-based and correlation-aware FDIA that remains stealthy under AC state estimation and bypasses bad data detection (BDD) by explicitly incorporating spatio-temporal dependencies among nodal injections. The attack strategy employs a reduced-dimensional measurement matrix and an error covariance matrix to model injection correlations, thereby minimizing operational constraint violations. Correspondingly, a coupled Cubature Kalman Filter approach is characterized to enhance state estimation accuracy and reduce conservatism. To counter such evolving attacks, a deep reinforcement learning (DRL)-based detection mechanism is developed. Extensive validation on IEEE 14, 30, 57, and 118-bus systems demonstrates the effectiveness and robustness with 99.92%−100% accuracy of the proposed method.

title: Leveraging Heterogeneous Railway Systems as Virtual Inertia Sources for Grid Frequency Regulation
abstract: The expanding penetration of inverter-based renewable energy generation has significantly reduced grid inertia, intensifying frequency stability challenges in modern power systems. Correspondingly, large-scale electrified railway systems, which are conventionally viewed as passive loads, possess a substantial, yet largely unexploited, resource of kinetic energy with inherent potential to support grid frequency. To harness this potential, this paper proposes a hierarchical two-stage control framework that reconceptualizes railway fleets as active, deterministic, and dispatchable sources of virtual inertia, turning the kinetic energy inherent in train operation into a resource for grid stability. This framework integrates day-ahead stochastic scheduling of train trajectories with real-time hierarchical control, featuring a centralized Model Predictive Control (MPC) layer at the train dispatch center for global coordination and decentralized local controllers on individual trains for rapid inertial response. A cornerstone of this work is the explicit quantification of the virtual inertia available from each train as a function of its physical momentum. This quantification supports a fine-grained control strategy for heterogeneous fleets, accommodating both high-inertia, flexible freight trains and agile passenger trains with tight scheduling constraints. This adaptive approach maximizes grid support while preserving transportation service quality. Case study results validate the efficacy of the proposed strategy, demonstrating a 57.6% reduction in maximum frequency deviation under high-volatility conditions and an improvement of the frequency nadir by over 1.1 Hz during severe generation loss events, thereby preventing emergency load-shedding. Ultimately, this work establishes a scalable pathway for the synergistic operation of transport and power systems, unlocking an advanced class of controllable loads for resilient grid stabilization.

title: Exact Analytical Solution for Self-Scheduling of Energy Storage With Piecewise Objective and Energy Loss Functions
abstract: The optimal self-scheduling (OSS) problem is fundamental to the economic operation of energy storage resources. Accurately modeling their nonlinear characteristics, such as complementarity constraints or state-dependent efficiency, poses significant computational challenges. To attain tractability, most relevant studies rely on linear or convex approximations, leading to suboptimal operation decisions. To address this challenge, this paper proposes an efficient analytical solution method to exactly solve a generic formulation of OSS (G-OSS) with piecewise quadratic objective functions and piecewise linear loss functions, which can model a wide spectrum of practical energy storage with high fidelity. G-OSS is recast as a sequence of single-period parametric programs, and a generalized analytical solution algorithm (G-ASA) is devised to compute closed-form, piecewise-defined optimal solutions via a backward-forward framework. Theoretical analysis guarantees the global optimality of G-ASA for solving G-OSS. Numerical results validate that the G-ASA exhibits high efficiency and scalability, substantially outperforming the prevailing solver-based methods while ensuring global optimality.

title: DRL Energy Management for URT Considering Uncertainties of PV and Train Disturbance
abstract: Integrating photovoltaic (PV) energy into urban rail transit faces challenges due to PV variability and fluctuating train loads, often leading to low PV utilization. This paper proposes a deep reinforcement learning (DRL)-based energy management strategy that dynamically coordinates reversible converters to intelligently redistribute surplus PV energy across multiple power supply sections. The approach incorporates stochastic PV generation and train operation uncertainties into the training process within a Markov decision framework, and leverages day-ahead optimization results to design a time-varying reward mechanism that guides real-time control at per second time. Simulation studies on Qingdao Metro Line 2 show that the proposed method achieves a 4.15% reduction in annual energy consumption, corresponding to 1.7 GWh, and outperforms recent optimization-based methods. To further verify real-time feasibility and control effectiveness, a hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) platform using a reduced-scale metro line is developed, on which the trained DRL agent is deployed and shown to achieve energy saving in real-time tests. These results highlight the method’s ability to improve energy efficiency and facilitate greater integration of PV energy under dynamic and uncertain conditions in urban rail transit.

title: An Economic Scheduling Strategy for Multi-Microgrid Distribution System Based on Bi-Level Flexibility Trading Mechanism
abstract: Coordinating distribution-local flexibility trading with multi-microgrid (MMG) scheduling offers an effective approach to managing distributed energy resources (DERs). However, existing scheduling strategies based on traditional flexibility trading mechanisms (FTMs) struggle to fully unlock the flexibility potential of DERs, leading to reduced overall economic efficiency. To address this issue, this paper proposes an economic scheduling strategy based on a new bi-level FTM for a multi-microgrid distribution system (MMDS). First, a bi-level FTM is designed. By peer-to-peer (P2P) and microgrid-to-distribution (M2D) flexibility trading, this bi-level FTM enables direct one-to-one flexibility transactions among all participants. On this basis, an economic scheduling strategy for MMG cooperation is proposed by fully considering flexibility regulation initiative and fair benefit allocation. Finally, case studies demonstrate that the proposed strategy effectively enhances resource utilization, economic performance, and stakeholder coordination within the MMDS.

title: Benchmarking the Robustness of Energy Management to Digital Implementation
abstract: The digital implementation of any energy management program faces discrepancies between continuously evolving physical variables (energy, temperature) and discretely executed automation routines: discrepancies are also inevitable between the ground-truth system and the control-oriented dynamics used to make the energy management real-time tractable. This work provides a theoretical and numerical framework to study robustness of digitally implemented energy management to such discrepancies. The theoretical challenge solved by our robustness framework lies in analytically handling rather general and possibly time-varying energy management problems operating digitally under a wide range of discrepancies. The analytical existence of robustness margins is confirmed via a numerical energy benchmark we introduce and for which control-oriented dynamics are derived. Numerical comparisons under established digitization strategies show that, despite modeling errors ranging in 6-52% and discretization errors ranging in 2-23%, the performance of model-based energy management (implemented via linear quadratic control) is more robust than rule-based or proportional-integral-derivative energy management. Such results are consistently verified under different sampling times, automation and grid-interactive demand response scenarios.

title: Conditional Distributionally Robust Optimization for Look-Ahead Power Dispatch With Heterogeneous Uncertainties
abstract: This paper presents a look-ahead environmental-economic power dispatch model incorporating heterogeneous uncertainties. A novel distributionally robust dispersion control is integrated in the model for managing air pollutant emissions. This control approach captures the spatial and temporal distribution of emissions, aiming to minimize their contribution to air pollutant concentrations. Furthermore, the dispersion condition uncertainty is modeled on a finite support to enhance control robustness. As a result, the traditional infinite-support renewable energy uncertainty is combined with the proposed finite-support dispersion condition uncertainty in a distributionally robust optimization framework. A joint ambiguity set is thus formulated for the two heterogeneous and correlative uncertainties, which addresses the heterogeneity through conditional probability theory and captures the correlation by conditional expectation constraints. To solve the distributionally robust dispatch model, it is first converted into a tractable form that incorporates robust cost constraints, utilizing dual theory of infinite dimensional linear programming. A conditional column and constraint generation method is then developed to tackle the reformulated problem. Numerical simulations demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed dispersion control in improving air quality, and the computational efficiency of our solution methods.

title: On the Solvability of the Power Flow Equation of DC Microgrids Under Distributed Control Through an Infinite Union Method
abstract: For a DC microgrid with constant power loads (CPLs), the existence of feasible power flow solutions is a necessary condition for correct system operation, which is often challenging to solve. This paper analyzes the solvability of the power flow equation for a meshed DC microgrid, where some distributed generations (DGs) are under distributed consensus control (DCC-DGs) to achieve current sharing and voltage regulation, while other DGs are under MPPT control (MPPT-DGs). Firstly, the power flow equation of the DC microgrid is established. Secondly, for the solvability of the power flow equation, an infinite union method based on Brouwer’s fixed point theorem is proposed. Compared with existing results, the derived solvability condition provides a larger feasible region for the loads. Furthermore, the derived solvability condition not only guarantees the existence of power flow solutions but also allows for acceptable nodal voltage deviations and safe output currents.
