This study assesses the impact of key economic and environmental factors on economic development, emphasising the role of green growth as an effective means to achieve sustainable development. Specifically, it examines the effect of greenfield investment (GFI), geopolitical risk (GPR), natural resources (TNR), and renewable energy consumption (GET) on green growth (GG) across 17 emerging economies from 2003 to 2022. Utilising advanced panel estimation techniques, the study concludes that GFI and GET contribute positively to green growth, whereas GPR adversely affects green growth. Similarly, the greater dependence on natural resources significantly hampers green growth, thereby confirming the presence of the ‘resource curse’ hypothesis in our analysis. Moreover, the interaction between GPR and TNR significantly dampens green growth, while the interaction between GPR and GFI further exacerbates this adverse effect. Based on these results, the study suggests that policymakers should promote greenfield investment in sustainable sectors, strengthen natural resource management through robust regulations, and mitigate geopolitical risk by diversifying international partnerships to support long-term sustainable development goals.

title: Enhancing Resilience of Power Distribution Systems Under Cyber-Physical Hybrid Attacks: A Coordinated Localization and Restoration Strategy With Feeder Automation
abstract: The widespread deployment of distributed feeder automation (DFA) has increased the vulnerability of power distribution systems to cyber-physical hybrid attacks. To enhance the resilience of power distribution systems under hybrid attacks, this paper proposes a two-stage integrated cyber-physical system (TICPS) recovery strategy. This strategy integrates hybrid attack localization and isolation, and cyber-physical collaborative restoration, while effectively coordinating multiple resources. In the first stage, a hybrid attack localization module is developed, incorporating an attack descriptive model and a network equivalent transformation method to accurately locate cyber and physical attacks. The localization results are then used to guide DFA to isolate attacked agents and line faults resulting from the attacks. In the second stage, a grid reconfiguration and island formation module is first proposed to achieve efficient load restoration while considering the operational constraints of DFA under a compromised cyber layer. Subsequently, a repair crew dispatch module is designed to optimize crew routing based on value functions of cyber-physical faulty components, thereby facilitating complete cyber-physical system recovery. To leverage sequentially restored and controllable resources during the repair process, a repair event-triggered mechanism is introduced to coordinate grid reconfiguration and crew dispatch. The effectiveness and scalability of the proposed strategy are validated through simulations on the IEEE 33-bus and IEEE 123-bus systems, which demonstrate promising results.

title: Robust Observer-Enhanced Resilient Control of Grid-Following LCL Inverters Under Cyber Sensor Attacks
abstract: This paper presents a robust proportional–integral (PI) control strategy with an observer for grid-following (GFL) inverters modeled as cyber–physical systems (CPS), designed to withstand denial-of-service (DoS) and intentional electromagnetic interference (IEMI) attacks targeting sensors and controllers. Such attacks can corrupt sensor measurements, cause communication delays and outages, degrade control performance, and even destabilize the system. In contrast to existing control approaches, the proposed method explicitly mitigates the detrimental effects of both DoS and IEMI attacks. The observer and PI controller gains are co-designed using linear matrix inequality (LMI) based optimization, ensuring robust stability under attack scenarios. Control and estimation processes are implemented within a time-triggered framework to guarantee deterministic timing and enable rigorous stability analysis. Furthermore, a residual-based fault and attack detection scheme employing fixed thresholds and hysteresis is introduced to promptly identify and isolate compromised sensors or communication links. Once an attack is detected, the system switches to healthy measurements or substitutes observer estimates to preserve stable operation. The effectiveness of the proposed approach is validated through real-time hardware experiments and MATLAB/Simulink simulations using a laboratory-scale grid-connected inverter. The results demonstrate the method’s strong resilience and stability against IEMI and DoS attacks compared with conventional control strategies.

title: A Behavioral-Strategic Market Mechanism for Energy Sharing: Integrating LLM-Driven Bounded Rationality With Regulatory Optimization
abstract: Energy sharing markets facilitate collaborative energy exchange among prosumers, yet their theoretical efficiency is often compromised by bounded rationality. Existing regulatory mechanisms, predicated on the assumption of perfect rationality, mathematically mask this non-linear cognitive friction, leaving grid operators vulnerable to unstructured behavioral instabilities. To bridge this gap, we propose a Bi-Level Regulatory Optimization Framework that integrates Large Language Models (LLMs) as a “surrogate behavioral stress-testing” environment. Unlike traditional models that rely on static utility functions, the lower level employs Neuro-Symbolic Agents to inject heuristic-driven bounded rationality, acting as a sandbox that exposes latent market vulnerabilities ignored by convex optimization. The upper level utilizes derivative-free Bayesian Optimization (BO) to autonomously navigate this non-differentiable cognitive feedback and discover a deterrence-based regulatory policy. Empirical evaluations using the real-world physical net-load dataset from Madeira Island substantiate the framework’s efficacy. The experiments validate that the optimized dynamic volatility tax operates effectively via deterrence, steering heuristic agents to voluntarily correct cognitive failures (e.g., converting speculative trading into a strategic retreat). This mechanism achieves a robust market equilibrium, reducing price volatility ( $\sigma _{\lambda }$ ) by 84.6% and successfully withstanding the unstructured behavioral unpredictability inherent in decentralized energy communities.

title: Distributed Resilient Power Control Strategy Against Data Injection Attacks in Wind Farms
abstract: With the increasing proportion of installed wind power capacity in the power grid, higher requirements are put forward for the cyber security technology of wind energy enterprises. However, due to problems such as incomplete construction and unstrict requirements, there exist many blind spots of cyber security in the current power monitoring system of wind energy enterprises. Data injection attacks targeting the communication pathway between the supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) system and the wind turbines will degrade the power generation of wind farms and lead to an imbalance in the power supply to the grid. To this end, this paper attempts to propose an observation and compensation based distributed resilient power control strategy to resist data injection attacks in the wind farm. The data injection threat model is formulated to characterize the behavior of tampering with the power information of wind turbines reported to the local controller and SCADA system, and an adaptive observer is proposed to observe the injected value in real-time, guiding the wind farm to balance the power generation. A distributed resilient power control strategy is developed to ensure the dynamic balance of expected power generation and the secure operation of wind farms. Extensive studies on a wind farm consisting of 9 wind turbines verify that the proposed method can eliminate the impact of data injection attacks and ensure the expected control performance of the wind farm.

title: Beyond Energy Trading: AI-Enhanced Peer-to-Peer Energy Bartering
abstract: Peer-to-peer energy trading supports efficient utilization of renewable energy but fails to address energy poverty and financial transaction barriers, particularly during economic or infrastructural crises. Consumers may lack funds or means to purchase energy or face difficulties in making transactions for various reasons, while producers may struggle to sell surplus energy through conventional markets. To overcome these challenges, energy bartering offers a promising non-monetary alternative by facilitating direct energy exchange among peers within smart grid environments. This paper proposes AI-P2P-EB, a novel artificial intelligence-enhanced peer-to-peer energy bartering algorithm that improves producer profitability and drives broader participation in decentralized energy systems. Three bartering algorithms and their influencing factors across two scenarios were analyzed. Using two real-world datasets, it is demonstrated that the studied bartering algorithms reduced reliance on the utility grid, saving up to 1,310 megawatt-hours, and bartered between 3.8 megawatt-hours to 1.9 gigawatt-hours. Energy bartering maximizes monetary benefits for peers when the grid does not buy all surplus energy. In contrast, when the grid buys surplus, consumer benefits outweigh producer gains, except in the centralized approach. Our findings categorize energy transactions based on driving incentives and demonstrate the superior performance of the AI-enhanced algorithm in increasing producer profits while maintaining a high amount of bartered energy.

title: Cost-Aware Detection and Mitigation of Charge Manipulation Attacks in Electric Vehicle Aggregations
Infrequent Control of Thermostatically Controlled Loads for Fast Power System Services
abstract: Controlling electric load aggregations enables the demand side to provide services to the grid. However, the feedback and actuation update rates of these loads could be limited by technical constraints. In this paper, we consider a frequency regulation application with thermostatically controlled loads, in which the underlying devices can only send feedback and be actuated at a rate that is slower than the reference signal being tracked. We develop a control approach to maximize the potential for providing fast power system services with limited feedback and actuation frequency. This approach balances computational effort and tracking accuracy by utilizing an aggregate representation of the controlled devices in a quadratic programming optimization problem. The trade-off between computational effort and tracking accuracy is explored by using a second much more complex controller that considers the dynamics of individual devices. The impact of imperfect reference signal forecasts is also analyzed.

title: Fuzzy Deep Reinforcement Learning-Based Space–Air–Ground Integration for Electric Power Emergency Communication
abstract: With the advancement of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and artificial intelligence, space-air-ground integration reshapes electric power emergency communication through coordinated resource scheduling. However, existing learning-based resource scheduling has slow convergence, local optimality, and poor quantifiable interpretability. In this paper, we propose a fuzzy deep reinforcement learning-based resource scheduling design, aiming to maximize the weighted sum of inspection and coverage utility minus backhaul delay cost by optimizing UAV path planning, backhaul routing, and flow control. It develops a multi-agent interactive deep fuzzy neuro actor critic mechanism for collaborative 3D path planning and a backpressure-aware approach for multi-hop data backhaul. Simulations in flooding areas show its superiority in real-time situational awareness, on-demand coverage, and fast inspection.

title: Microgrid Under-Frequency Load Shedding Strategy Integrating LMC-Shapley Value and Knowledge Distillation
abstract: As the final safeguard for maintaining microgrid stability, under-frequency load shedding (UFLS) can effectively prevent rapid frequency drops caused by system faults. However, a key challenge remains in how to fairly and effectively allocate load shedding across nodes to enhance overall system resilience. To address this issue, this paper proposes a microgrid UFLS strategy that integrates Shapley value with load multiplicity characteristics (LMC-Shapley) and knowledge distillation. The strategy first constructs a node contribution factor based on the load importance, economic loss from load shedding and frequency regulation effect. Then, based on the LMC-Shapley value method, the marginal contributions and allocation coefficients of each indicator are calculated to determine the load shedding amount for each node. To mitigate the computational complexity introduced by the LMC-Shapley method, a model lightweighting method based on knowledge distillation is proposed, allowing transfer of complex knowledge from a teacher model to a student model. Finally, based on the improved IEEE-37 node system microgrid model, the performance of the proposed strategy is verified. Simulation results reveal that the proposed strategy exhibits good frequency recovery performance.

title: Optimal Integrated Satellite-Terrestrial Network Design for Microgrid Clusters Under Wildfires
abstract: Wildfires pose a critical threat to microgrid clusters especially in mountainous and remote areas, degrading communication infrastructures and destroying system stability. To address this issue, this paper proposes a wildfire-oriented communication network design for resilient operation of microgrid clusters based on an integrated satellite-terrestrial network (ISTN). First, a disaster-aware reliability assessment model is developed to describe communication link availability by explicitly coupling wildfire evolution with link failure mechanisms. Second, based on the wildfire-induced link availability obtained from the reliability assessment model, a topology restoration model is formulated to maximize algebraic connectivity under limited satellite terminal deployment constraints, and an alternating optimization strategy based on the Fiedler vector (ALT-Fiedler) is proposed to solve the resulting mixed-integer spectral optimization problem. Third, based on the restored topology, a communication weight optimization model is established to characterize the trade-off between convergence performance and delay robustness, which is reformulated as a semidefinite programming problem (SDP) for solution. Finally, simulation results validate that the proposed method effectively restores communication connectivity under wildfire conditions with limited satellite terminals and enables reliable coordinated operation of microgrid clusters.

title: Learning a Unified Feasibility--Cost Interface for Heterogeneous Flexible Resources
abstract: With the rapid proliferation of heterogeneous flexible resources (HFRs), such as microgrids and virtual power plants, hierarchical dispatch has become essential, making aggregate modeling a crucial foundation for resource coordination. Existing methods typically decouple the aggregate feasible region (AFR) of HFRs from the aggregate cost function (ACF). This separation isolates physical constraints from economic signals, preventing operators from quantifying the marginal value of flexibility and causing modeling redundancy. To solve this, we propose a feasibility-embedded aggregate cost function, unifying feasibility and cost into a strictly convex scalar interface. First, by implicitly representing physical limits as steep economic penalties, we recast the decoupled aggregation of AFR and ACF into a unified fitting problem. Second, a tailored multi-scale input-convex neural network is developed to resolve the inherent conflict between approximating smooth operational costs and capturing sharp feasibility barriers. Numerical results validate that the proposed interface achieves superior accuracy while maintaining a highly compact formulation.

title: Reconnection-Time-Optimal Fractional-Chaotic SIR-Gossip Control for Resilient Microgrid Islanding and Reconnection
abstract: The rapid growth of distributed renewable generation and inverter-based resources has heightened the need for control strategies that guarantee both safety and freshness during microgrid islanding and reconnection, such as those used in real-time dynamic network environments. In the specific scenario of microgrid reconnection, existing schemes like randomized gossip, asynchronous gossip, and fractional-order consensus can not effectively exploit fractional memory and trust-SIR dynamics, leading to slow convergence and high reconnection time. In this paper, we propose a unified fractional-chaotic susceptible-infected-recovered (SIR)-Gossip controller (UFSC) to solve the existing problem of minimizing reconnection time while ensuring safety, integrity, and freshness. By optimizing the closed-form exponents and utilizing a co-designed framework of trust recovery, risk expansion, and consensus acceleration, our approach achieves provably minimal reconnection time and superior consensus accuracy. The experiment results demonstrate the advantages of our approach in improving reconnection time by up to 46% and reducing consensus error by up to 30%, outperforming traditional methods in terms of synchronization, trust recovery, and overall system performance.

title: Condition-Driven Direct-to-Satellite Multi-UAV Inspection for Offshore Wind Farms
abstract: With the expansion of offshore wind farms, the complex maritime conditions and harsh offshore environments pose challenges to routine inspections, including limited communication connectivity and poor response timeliness. In this article, a condition-driven direct-to-satellite multi-UAV inspection scheme is proposed. Deviating from conventional geometry-based routing, a novel prioritization mechanism is developed to intrinsically couple the anomalous electrical states of offshore wind turbines (OWTs) with spatial flight geometries. The scheme further improves operational efficiency by optimizing UAV trajectories under a priority-consistent sensor wake-up mapping for minimum inspection time. However, the formulated optimization problem is inherently a nonconvex mixed-integer nonlinear program (MINLP) with an unknown number of time slots, which makes conventional methods ineffective. To overcome this challenge, the problem is reformulated as a Markov decision process (MDP), and a K-means pre-partitioned soft actor-critic (KP-SAC) algorithm is developed to efficiently search for high-quality solutions. Simulation results verify that the proposed method significantly reduces inspection completion time compared with the baseline schemes under diverse sensing-load settings and communication conditions. From an offshore wind farm operation perspective, the post-processing evaluation demonstrates that reduced inspection completion time enables earlier inspection-triggered intervention, with shorter periods of degraded operating conditions and curtailed available output.

title: Field-calibrated surrogate prediction and uncertainty-aware decision diagnostics for multi-unit geothermal organic Rankine cycle plants
The role of aggregated EV battery storage in managing future load peaks: A New York state case study
Global sensitivity analysis of optimal capacity planning for green ammonia production under grid dependency and energy curtailment constraints
Low-carbon collaborative scheduling of industrial microgrids with electrolytic aluminum load considering electricity-carbon trading
A Device‐to‐Package Perspective on Thermal Management Materials for Electronic Devices
abstract: ABSTRACT With the continued miniaturization and integration of electronic devices, power density and local heat flux have increased substantially, making heat dissipation a major constraint on device performance and reliability. Improving thermal transport inside devices through materials engineering has therefore attracted increasing attention. In this review, we systematically summarize the thermal transport mechanisms, recent progress, and manipulation strategies of materials for thermal management of electronic devices along the internal heat‐dissipation pathway. At the device and die level, we discuss representative semiconductors, metals, and dielectrics, with emphasis on their thermal transport mechanisms and their thermal conductivity manipulation. In addition, thermal transport across microscopic interfaces is discussed. At the package level, we focus on thermal interface materials (TIMs) with emphasis on their structure–property relationships and thermal performance enhancement strategies. Across these different levels, a common principle emerges: intrinsic thermal conductivity alone is insufficient to determine the thermal performance of a material after integration, because dimensions, processing‐induced changes, and interfaces are also important. By analyzing materials along the internal heat‐dissipation pathway, this review identifies the key thermal bottlenecks and defines the material and interface requirements for a low‐resistance internal heat‐dissipation pathway in future electronic devices with high power density and a high degree of integration.

title: Submolecular Selenium Enables Low‐Pressure and Recyclable All‐Solid‐State Li–Se Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT All‐solid‐state lithium‐selenium (Li–Se) batteries offer high energy density and intrinsic safety, but their practical deployment is hindered by sluggish solid‐state redox kinetics, large volume fluctuations, and unstable solid‐solid interfaces, particularly under low stack pressure. Here we report a submolecular Se x cathode by converting crystalline cyclo‐Se 8 into amorphous single‐atom and short‐chain Se (Se x , x x @G), which increases the electronic conductivity from 6.3 × 10 −5 to 13 S cm −1 and Li + diffusivity from 1.7 × 10 −14 to 2.0 × 10 −11 cm 2 s −1 . Meanwhile, a Li 2 O‐nanoshell‐modified sulfide solid electrolyte is designed to stabilize the interface against both Li metal and Se cathode. As a result, all‐solid‐state Li–Se batteries deliver the theoretical capacity of 673 mAh g −1 at 0.1 C and retain 86% capacity over 2800 cycles at 3 C under 8 MPa, with stable operation down to −30°C. All‐solid‐state Li–Se pouch cells further achieve an energy density of 420 Wh kg −1 and 94% capacity retention after 300 cycles under 2.5 MPa. Post‐mortem analysis reveals that the submolecular Se x species are not only structurally preserved but also recyclable after electrochemical cycling within the solid‐state reaction environment. This work establishes submolecular chalcogen chemistry as a new design paradigm for low‐pressure, recyclable, and high‐energy all‐solid‐state batteries.

title: Chemically Reactivatable Sulfide Interfaces for Low‐Pressure Thick‐Cathode Solid‐State Na–S Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Low‐pressure solid‐state Na–S batteries with thick sulfur cathodes are attractive for high‐energy storage, but their operation is fundamentally constrained by the progressive loss of solid–solid contact during sulfur conversion. Once insulating sulfides become poorly connected to the electronic network, charge recovery becomes incomplete and cathode passivation rapidly accumulates. Here, we construct chemically reactivatable sulfide interfaces by embedding Fe 3 C–MnO heteropoints within nitrogen‐doped hollow carbon nanotubes. The heterointerface integrates carbon‐side electronic coupling, sulfide‐side affinity, and interfacial polarization, thereby suppressing localized sulfide accumulation and sustaining charge‐stage sulfur recovery as mechanical confinement weakens. This effect is strongly pressure dependent. Under high compression, the electrochemical responses of different hosts converge, whereas under contact‐limited conditions the Fe 3 C–MnO architecture preserves markedly higher sulfur utilization, lower polarization, and superior cycling stability. Consequently, the operational pressure required to retain ≥80% of the 10 MPa discharge capacity decreases from approximately 2 MPa for the control cathodes to 0.2 MPa for Fe 3 C–MnO/NC@S. A 200 µm cathode with 8.3 mg cm −2 sulfur sustains reversible cycling at 0.2 MPa, together with a pouch‐cell energy density of 696 Wh kg cathode −1 . These results establish sulfide‐interface reactivation as a route to decouple reversible sulfur chemistry from stringent mechanical confinement.

title: Realizing Reversible Photo‐Charging via Stacked 1T/2H MoS 2 Bifunctional Cathodes for Photo‐Rechargeable Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Photo‐rechargeable batteries that integrate solar energy harvesting, conversion, and storage in a single device are able to efficiently utilize sustainable energy. However, current photo‐batteries based on bifunctional (photovoltaic conversion and energy storage) cathodes could only achieve photo‐assisted charging, whereas light‐only photo‐charging remains incomplete and irreversible. Particularly, in absence of a photo‐charging circuit, the observed charging phenomena are pseudo photo‐charging due to side reactions. To realize genuine photo‐charging, we design a bifunctional cathode of MoS 2 by integrating photo active (2H) and energy storage (1T) phases. Nickel oxide is introduced to improve the interface conductivity and stabilize the 2H/1T phases of MoS 2 . Additionally, we employed an external resistance to balance the self‐discharge current and the photo‐charging current under illumination. For the first time, we demonstrate Zn 2+ photo‐batteries that can be reversibly photo‐charged for over ten times, and the deposition of zinc at the anode is visualized. The photo‐rechargeable batteries could realize a photo‐charging capacity ratio of 100% by2 h illumination, with a specific capacity of 110.55 mAh g −1 . Furthermore, we assemble a sustainable energy harvest‐conversion‐storage mini‐system that could practically provide energy to portable electronics.

title: Re(I)‐Based Molecular Actuator‐Equipped Nanomotors for Integrated Photodynamic and Photomechanical Therapy of Solid Tumor
abstract: ABSTRACT The dense stromal barrier of solid tumors severely hinders intratumoral distribution and therapeutic performance of conventional nanomedicines, and such limitation further compromises oxygen‐dependent photodynamic therapy. Herein, through molecular engineering, we develop a Janus nanomotor ( Re1@NMs ) that integrates a three‐dimensional rhenium(I)‐based molecular actuator ( Re1 ) with glucose oxidase (GOx)‐powered propulsion. Owing to the Janus structure, asymmetric GOx‐catalyzed glucose consumption generates local chemical gradients that fuel autonomous motility, thereby enhancing intratumoral distribution. Upon light activation, the engineered Re1 , screened from six Re(I) complexes, functions both as a dual Type I/II photosensitizer generating reactive oxygen species (ROS) to induce oxidative stress and as a molecular actuator whose Y ‐axis motif undergoes E / Z photoisomerization and torsional deformation, thereby contributing to membrane permeabilization. The resulting integrated mechano‐photodynamic action coordinately activates ferroptosis and pyroptosis. In a murine tumor model, Re1@NMs ‐mediated phototherapy achieves superior tumor suppression with excellent biosafety and further elicits robust antitumor immunity, as evidenced by enhanced dendritic cell maturation, increased tumor‐infiltrating T cells, elevated effector cytokine expression, and damage‐associated molecular pattern release. To the best of our knowledge, this work represents the first integration of a deliberately engineered metal‐complex‐based three‐dimensional molecular actuator with a tumor‐microenvironment‐adaptive nanomotor, establishing a new paradigm for overcoming tumor barriers.

title: A Stable Terminal Mercury Hydride and Its Reactivity To Form Mercury–Metal Bonds
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Organomercury hydrides are typically encountered as unstable intermediates in organic transformations. These compounds are conventionally thought to be intrinsically unstable and have eluded isolation in the condensed phase. Here, we report the synthesis, isolation, characterization, and reactivity of an unexpectedly stable arylmercury hydride using a sterically encumbering fluorenyl-hydrindacene scaffold. The arylmercury hydride readily reacts with metalloradicals and metal hydrides to form bimetallic complexes containing unsupported mercury–metal bonds. These results suggest that the instability of mercury hydride compounds is not due to an intrinsic weakness of the mercury–hydrogen bond, but rather their propensity to undergo bimetallic reactions that result in mercury–mercury bond formation.

title: Unlocked Covalent Competition in Asymmetric La/Sr‐O‐Fe Motif Activates Lattice Oxygen for Selective Methane Oxidation
abstract: ABSTRACT Controlling lattice‐oxygen reactivity in transition‐metal (TM) oxides is essential for Mars‐van Krevelen selective oxidations, yet conventional strategies that tune TM 1 ‐O‐TM 2 bridges suffer from covalent competition between adjacent redox‐active cations, which generates site heterogeneity and degrades selectivity. Herein, taking Ruddlesden–Popper LaSrFeO 4 (A 2 BO 4 ) as a model, we demonstrate that constructing asymmetric A‐O‐B motifs (i.e., La‐O‐Fe and Sr‐O‐Fe) provides a distinct route to overcome this limitation. Combined experiments and DFT calculations reveal that the A‐O‐B configuration could convert redox‐inert A‐site cations into direct electronic contributors to oxygen, which unlocks the covalent competition, substantially enabling promoted electron density over oxygen and enhanced Fe─O bond covalency. Consequently, LaSrFeO 4 displays much lower methane activation barrier (∼1.24 eV) than its perovskite counterpart, LaFeO 3, with an Fe‐O‐Fe motif (1.90 eV), ultimately affording a 2.35‐fold increase in syngas yield with 97% selectivity. This discovery reveals that asymmetric A‐O‐B coordination may serve as a promising structural strategy, distinct from B‐O‐B modulation, for modulating the electronic properties and reactivity of lattice oxygen.

title: Boosting Efficient Water Oxidation via Photothermal‐Enhanced High‐Entropy Oxides With Dual AEM and LOM Pathways
abstract: ABSTRACT High‐entropy oxides (HEOs) with photothermal conversion capability provide a promising platform for enhancing the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) in electrocatalytic water splitting. In this work, the adsorbate evolution mechanism (AEM), the lattice oxygen mechanism (LOM), and photothermal effects are integrated into a single reaction system through Fe doping into HEOs. By combining theoretical calculations and experimental characterizations, we reveal that Fe doping optimally tailors the adsorption/desorption energetics of intermediates along the AEM, while simultaneously introducing oxygen vacancies that modulate the metal‐oxygen electronic environment and promote LOM participation. This dual‐pathway activation, enabled by the high‐entropy rock‐salt structure, enhances catalytic activity. In addition, the photothermal effect of (FeMgCoNiCuZn)O 1−x can accelerate interfacial charge‐transfer kinetics and facilitate OOH * deprotonation. Under Xe‐lamp irradiation, Fe doping lowers the apparent activation energy for OER from 15.3 to 11.2 kJ mol −1 , and the catalyst achieves oxygen evolution current densities of 10 and 50 mA cm −2 at overpotentials of 159 and 247 mV. More importantly, it exhibits outstanding long‐term durability, maintaining stable operation for over 1500 h at 1 A cm −2 . These findings underscore the potential of Fe‐doping hexanary HEOs as a highly efficient candidate for electrocatalytic water splitting.

title: Single- and few-layer materials: synthesis, structure–property relationships, integration of AI/ML, and energy storage applications
Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy for proton exchange membrane fuel cells: From implementation to application
abstract: Proton exchange membrane fuel cells play a vital role in achieving a hydrogen-powered, carbon-neutral society. Although they have been deployed in stationary and transportation applications, their limited durability and reliability still restrict large-scale commercialization. Assessing internal health states is critical to overcoming these challenges by preventing operational faults and minimizing degradation rates. However, hydrogen fuel cells are highly nonlinear, multiscale, and multiphysics systems, hindering the estimation of system health states. This review investigates a nondestructive and in situ characterization technique, electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS), to characterize the health states of hydrogen fuel cells. The variation in internal health states is directly reflected in the impedance spectrum, which can be assessed through proper interpretation. Nevertheless, developing EIS for hydrogen fuel cells is a nontrivial task. Implementing and applying EIS requires interdisciplinary studies in signal processing, control theory, and machine learning in particular cases. This review systematically discusses the implementation, interpretation, and application of EIS for hydrogen fuel cells. The onboard applicability and short measurement time are key factors in EIS implementation. Model-based and DRT-based interpretation approaches are reviewed for efficiently extracting valuable health states. Based on these methods, the applications of EIS in performance characterization, fault diagnosis, degradation analysis, and prognostics are discussed. Four perspectives regarding general, non-electrical, localized, and multiphysics-integrated EIS, are proposed to highlight and guide EIS-related studies in hydrogen fuel cells. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the deployment and application of EIS in hydrogen fuel cells and offers insights into addressing durability and reliability challenges.

Distributed Fixed-Time Secondary Control for Microgrids With Communication Delays and Disturbances
abstract: The paper addresses the distributed secondary control (DSC) problem of the islanded microgrid composed of six distributed generators (DGs) with communication delay and external disturbances. Firstly, by utilizing the Artstein model reduction method, a distributed delay-compensated strategy is proposed to restore the voltage and frequency of each DG to reference values in a fixed time. Secondly, a novel sliding mode reaching law is designed to resist disturbances and accelerate convergence, thereby ensuring the sliding surface is reached within a fixed-time. Thirdly, the proposed approach integrates an event-triggered (ET) mechanism with an integral sliding mode surface, effectively conserving communication resources while avoiding Zeno behavior. In summary, the proposed delay-compensation strategy integrated with sliding mode control (SMC) guarantees the fixed-time synchronization of voltage and frequency for DGs with coordinated power sharing control. Finally, the simulation results validate the control strategy’s effectiveness, robustness to load changes, plug-and-play capability, and indicate that the proposed ET mechanism can greatly decrease communication frequency.

A performance-based framework for assessing underground hydrogen storage under reservoir and infrastructure constraints: Application to offshore wind curtailment mitigation
Multi-domain spectral feature fusion and ensemble learning for simultaneous online determination of vanadium concentration and SOC in VRFB positive electrolytes

Distributed small-reservoir pumped-storage hydropower in Europe: a GIS screening under drawdown and karst constraints
abstract: Continental pumped-storage hydropower (PSH) atlases omit schemes built from small reservoirs, although such sites could provide distributed flexibility. We screen this resource across 37 European countries, detecting closed depressions and water bodies and pairing upper and lower reservoirs under land-use, protection and grid-distance constraints. The reproducible workflow uses open pan-European data, a hybrid terrain stack (FABDEM; national lidar in Norway and Sweden) and an explicit allowable water-level variation for lake volume. At a 5-km grid distance and 1-m drawdown, exact maximum-weight matching gives an all-size screened bound of 2.57 TWh; excluding mapped-karst footprints for purpose-built reservoirs and sites above 2500 m leaves 0.58 TWh, of which a 21 115-site portfolio capped at 100 MWh per site stores 0.40 TWh (0.24 TWh, EU-27). Replacing FABDEM by national lidar cuts Norway’s and Sweden’s screened energy with 72% each (328.7 to 92.1 and 67.3 to 18.5 GWh): usable lake volume barely moves ( − 0.4 %), but pairs containing a dry basin collapse because that basin binds. A Sobol analysis makes maximum pair distance and karst treatment the joint controls (total effects 0.49 and 0.48). This is an exploratory first screening, not deployable capacity: it ranks where national feasibility studies should look, and their constraints can only reduce it.

Robust State Estimation for Distribution Systems Based on Reinforcement-Learning-Assisted Memory-Augmented Deep Kalman Filter
abstract: Real-time monitoring and control of distribution networks rely on robust state estimation. The key challenges lie in maintaining the accuracy, robustness, and computational efficiency of state estimation in the presence of bad measurement data and sudden changes in system states, particularly under limited sensor coverage. To overcome these challenges, this paper proposes a robust forecasting-aided state estimation method for distribution systems. The key methodology is a reinforcement-learning-assisted, memory-augmented, and gradient-fused deep Kalman filter. The proposed deep filter captures temporal patterns in state trajectories across multiple time steps, and fuses the prediction model’s gradient information into the state filtering stage for accurate uncertainty quantification. Based on normalized innovations, the proposed reinforcement learning-assisted method can also adjust the state filtering process to mitigate the impacts of bad data and state jumps on the estimation results with high efficiency. Extensive simulations are conducted on standard IEEE 34-node and 123-node test feeders with real-world load profiles and renewable generation data to demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed method in terms of estimation accuracy, robustness, and computational efficiency compared with a variety of state-of-the-art state estimation algorithms.

title: Fréchet Power-Scenario Distance: A Measure for Evaluating Synthetic Data Across Multiple Time-Scales in Smart Grids
abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence models for smart grids have advanced rapidly in recent years, and the synthetic data they produce can help mitigate limited data access caused by strict confidentiality constraints in power systems. A central challenge, however, is how to rigorously evaluate the quality of both the generative models and the synthetic time series they produce. Generic evaluation metrics are often not tailored to grid-specific requirements—such as multi-timescale temporal structure, cross-resolution consistency, and physically meaningful operating regimes—and therefore can yield misleading assessments. In this work, we propose a novel measure based on the Fréchet Distance (FD) estimated between two datasets in a power-centric learned feature space. Our approach embeds smart-grid time series using a hierarchical multi-resolution encoder trained on real grid data that encourages sensitivity to multi-timescale dynamics and resolution-consistent operational signatures. Across multiple use cases, the resulting Fr’echet Power-Scenario Distance (FPD) exposes temporal and physical mismatches more reliably and correlates with downstream task performance more strongly than conventional baselines, enabling more robust benchmarking of generative models for smart-grid data.

title: World-Model-Based Deep Reinforcement Learning for Real-Time Microgrid Energy Management
abstract: This paper proposes a model-based deep reinforcement learning (DRL) framework for microgrid energy management built on a Dreamer-style world model. The approach jointly learns a latent dynamics model of the microgrid and a continuous control policy, and uses multi-step imagination rollouts for prediction-based decision making under AC power-flow and operational constraints. Since actions are evaluated inside the learned model before being applied, operators can inspect predicted trajectories to see how decisions affect future costs and network states. The method is tested on three distribution-level microgrids. Across all cases, the proposed method achieves substantially higher sample efficiency than widely adopted model-free RL benchmarks, reaching near-asymptotic performance within a few thousand environment steps while these benchmarks require tens of thousands or fail to converge. The learned policies further achieve a favorable balance between operating cost and safety violations relative to state-of-the-art model-free and model-based RL baselines, approaching the performance of an idealized mixed integer programming-based benchmark with perfect foresight.

title: Distributed Quantized Control for Multiple DC Microgrids via Asymmetric Sampling Under Bandwidth Constraints
abstract: With the growing digitalization and networking of microgrids, limited bandwidth has become a critical constraint in practical implementation. This paper investigates the problem of distributed control for multiple DC microgrids under bandwidth constraints and proposes a novel control strategy based on dynamic quantization and asymmetric sampling mechanism. The dynamic quantization dynamically adjusts the quantization resolution, enabling efficient communication with as few as 1 bit per transmission, minimizing the required data volume. Meanwhile, the asymmetric sampling allows heterogeneous sampling rates for different generators, substantially decreasing the communication frequency. Unlike event-triggered methods, this strategy avoids the reliance on continuous monitoring devices, thereby enhancing practical feasibility. The proposed control strategy effectively achieves voltage regulation and current sharing among all distributed generators, while enabling power sharing across multiple microgrids under low-bandwidth conditions. Finally, the effectiveness is validated through RT-LAB, demonstrating a 64.43% reduction in bandwidth compared with the baseline event-triggered control strategy, while improving conventional bounded error to zero steady-state error.

title: Physics-Embedded Graph Convolutional Network With Topology-Adaptive Transfer Learning for Power Flow Prediction
abstract: Power flow prediction is a growing task in uncertain power system operation and analysis. Although data-driven models which apply machine learning techniques offer computational efficiency for power flow calculation, they often result in physically inconsistent solutions and exhibit poor generalization across different network topologies. This article proposes a physics-embedded graph convolutional network (PE-GCN) for physically consistent power flow prediction, and further develops a topology-adaptive transfer learning framework to improve generalization across different power network topologies. PE-GCN is developed based on a reformulated bus injection model (BIM) and embeds physical laws into the network architecture and training process. Specifically, hard constraints are enforced through a nodal power balance correction layer, and soft constraints are incorporated during training via a physics-regularized loss to enhance physical consistency. Building on PE-GCN, a topology-adaptive transfer learning framework with adversarial domain adaptation is introduced to improve generalization across network topologies and reduce the reliance on extensive labeled data under topology variations. Numerical studies on the IEEE-30, IEEE-118, and IEEE-300 bus systems validate the effectiveness of the proposed method in terms of prediction accuracy, physical consistency, computational efficiency, and adaptability to topology variations.

title: Privacy-Preserving Decision-Focused Learning for Multi-Energy Systems
abstract: Decision-making for multi-energy system (MES) dispatch depends on accurate load forecasting. Traditionally, load forecasting and decision-making for MES are implemented separately. Forecasting models are typically trained to minimize forecasting errors, overlooking their impact on downstream decision-making. To address this, decision-focused learning (DFL) has been studied to minimize decision-making costs instead. However, practical adoption of DFL in MES faces significant challenge: the process requires sharing sensitive load data and model parameters across multiple sectors, raising serious privacy issues. To this end, we propose a privacy-preserving DFL framework tailored for MES. Our approach introduces information masking to safeguard private data while enabling recovery of decision variables and gradients required for model training. To further enhance security for DFL, we design a safety protocol combining matrix decomposition and homomorphic encryption, effectively preventing collusion and unauthorized data access. Additionally, we develop a privacy-preserving load pattern recognition algorithm, that enables the training of specialized DFL models for heterogeneous load patterns. Theoretical analysis and case studies with real-world MES data, demonstrate that our framework not only protects privacy but also consistently achieves lower average daily dispatch costs compared to existing methods.

title: Nonlinear PDE-Constrained Optimal Dispatch of Gas and Power: A Global Linearization Approximation
abstract: The coordinated dispatch of power and gas is fundamental for the operational security of Electricity-Gas Integrated Energy Systems (EG-IES). However, the gas dynamics in the natural gas system (NGS) are governed by the nonlinear partial differential equations (PDE), making the dispatch problem of the EG-IES a complicated optimization model constrained by nonlinear PDE. Inaccurate modeling, such as the commonly used locally linearized model, can lead to operational limit violations in the NGS that might propagate and threaten the security of the coupled power system. To address it, we propose a globally linearized gas network model based on the Koopman operator theory. In particular, we propose a data-driven Koopman operator approximation approach for the globally linearized gas network model based on the extended dynamic mode decomposition, in which a physics-informed stability constraint is derived and embedded to improve generalization and accuracy. Based on this foundation, we develop an optimal dispatch model for the EG-IES. For the first time, this model explicitly incorporates the nonlinear gas dynamics governed by PDEs without resorting to local linearization or spatial discretization. The case study verifies the effectiveness of this work. Simulation results reveal that the commonly used locally linearized gas network model fails to accurately capture the dynamic characteristics of NGS, bringing potential security threats to the system.

title: A Unified Virtual Battery Modeling Framework for Flexibility Characterization of Building HVAC Systems
abstract: The heating, ventilation and air-conditioning (HVAC) systems dominate building’s energy consumption and meanwhile exhibit substantial operational flexibility that can be exploited for providing grid services. However, this goal is largely hindered by the difficulty to characterize the system’s operating flexibility due to the complex building thermal dynamics, physical operating limits and human comfort constraints. To address this challenge, this paper develops a unified virtual battery (VB) modeling framework for characterizing the operating flexibility of both single-zone and multi-zone building HVAC systems, enabling responsive buildings to function like virtual batteries. Specifically, a physically meaningful representation state is first identified to represent building thermal conditions under thermal comfort constraints and then a VB model is established for characterizing the operating flexibility of single-zone HVAC systems. We subsequently extend the VB modeling framework to multi-zone HVAC systems and establish zone VB models to characterize the heterogeneous zonal operating flexibility. We further develop a systematic method to aggregate the zone VB models into a unified VB model. The proposed VB model enables a low-order storage-like representation of the operational flexibility of both single-zone and multi-zone buildings. Case studies demonstrate that the VB model can well capture the building thermal dynamics under varying HVAC control policies. In addition, the VB model is validated through demand response (DR) of buildings. The optimal DR strategies can be obtained from the low-order and low-complexity VB model, and the building’s committed DR can be efficiently decomposed to zone-level control inputs while maintaining human thermal comfort.

title: Learning-Free Laplacian Kernel Modeling for Joint Imputation of Multi-Energy Load Data in Integrated Energy Systems
abstract: The reliability of data-driven applications in integrated energy systems (IESs), such as multi-energy load prediction, relies on the availability of complete and high-quality load data. However, real-world multi-energy load data can suffer from missing records, and accurate recovery remains challenging due to heterogeneous missing patterns and strong yet nontrivial coupling among different energy loads. To address this issue, this paper proposes an efficient learning-free Laplacian kernel framework for joint multi-energy load imputation, in which missing entries are directly treated as decision variables and the complete load matrix is reconstructed through a unified convex optimization formulation without requiring any training data. The proposed framework captures both the intra-load structure and cross-load coupling of multi-energy load data. This is achieved by combining a circulant Laplacian kernel-based temporal regularizer and a circulant tensor nuclear norm for local continuity and global periodicity, respectively, together with a correlation-based signed Laplacian regularizer for inter-load coupling relationship modeling. To efficiently solve the resulting optimization problem, an alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) algorithm is derived, where the dominant updates are implemented in the frequency domain via the fast Fourier transform (FFT) by exploiting the underlying circulant structures. This enables fast and scalable imputation of long-horizon and high-resolution load data with low computational overhead. Numerical experiments on real-world multi-energy load datasets demonstrate that the proposed framework not only consistently outperforms state-of-the-art imputation baselines under different missing patterns but also yields superior performance in downstream load forecasting tasks. The source code is available at: https://github.com/zhaopengfei12345/data-imputation

title: TFDA: A Time-Frequency Domain Adaptive Model for Multi-Source Multi-Task Anomaly Detection and Localization in Distribution Systems
abstract: Accurate anomaly detection and localization in distribution systems enable the timely event identification and the implementation of appropriate response strategies, which could minimize potential damage. However, many existing methods rely on extensive sensor data, requiring comprehensive measurement variables for data preprocessing and fusion, which limits their applicability in real-world scenarios. Moreover, prior methods often lack the necessary adaptive mechanisms to account for the variability of anomalies, which lead to inconsistent performance across tasks. To address these challenges, we propose a data-driven time-frequency domain adaptive model (TFDA) that incorporates both time-domain and frequency-domain features, only utilizing voltage magnitudes. The model introduces a spatial patch embedding block, which integrates sensor spatial information as graph priors and processes time-series data through patch-based operations to mitigate the impact of multi-resolution data. In the frequency-domain block, an adaptive thresholding technique is applied to eliminate less informative parts of the frequency spectrum. In the time-domain block, an adaptive weighting is utilized to balance the contributions of inter-channel and intra-channel anomaly information. We perform simulations on hardware-in-the-loop testbed to generate data that closely approximates real-world scenarios and demonstrate the superiority of our method over the baseline.

title: Output-to-Application Error Propagation in Neural Network-Based State Estimators for LV Grids
abstract: State estimation in low-voltage distribution grids is challenging due to limited measurement availability, unbalanced operation, and computational burden. While recent neural network-based estimators report high accuracy in voltage magnitude estimation, their reliability for downstream applications remains largely unexplored. This paper presents a multi-task neural network framework for estimating phase-to-ground voltage phasors in three-phase four-wire European-type unbalanced low-voltage grids using limited measurements. The reliability of such models is investigated not only in terms of the accuracy of predicted state variables but also in terms of the impact of estimation errors on derived electrical quantities. The results show that even small voltage estimation errors can lead to significant inaccuracies in derived power. Building on this insight, the neural network outputs are leveraged within a hybrid framework to initialize a conventional estimator, significantly reducing convergence time without compromising its accuracy. The findings reveal that accurate primary outputs do not necessarily guarantee reliable derived results, underscoring the need for evaluation strategies tailored to application-level requirements and the specific needs of each DSO. The article also addresses the question of whether models based exclusively on neural networks for this type of application can be considered complete state estimators or merely tools capable of providing acceptable estimates of certain electrical variables.

title: Distributed Dynamic Event-Triggered Secondary Control in Dually Heterogeneous Islanded PV--BESS Microgrids for Voltage--Frequency Regulation and SoC Balancing
abstract: High penetration of grid-following (GFL) PVs and grid-forming (GFM) storage/hybrid units creates islanded microgrids with dual heterogeneity in composition and control. In such systems, stochastic power injections from GFL units act as fast-varying disturbances to GFM units, which frequently violate fixed thresholds of conventional static event-triggered mechanisms, leading to excessive communication overhead. To address these challenges, this paper develops a fully distributed, dynamic event-triggered secondary control framework for dually heterogeneous microgrids. A unified controller achieves simultaneous frequency/voltage regulation, while ensuring accurate active power sharing and state-of-charge balancing exclusively for battery storage units. Importantly, a fully decentralized, graph-Laplacian-free dynamic triggering mechanism, synergized with local state predictors, is introduced. By employing an internal adaptive variable and relying solely on local states, this mechanism decouples event generation from communication topology, tolerating transient fluctuations without continuous neighbor monitoring. Lyapunov analysis guarantees global stability and excludes Zeno behavior. Hardware-in-the-loop tests validate that the proposed scheme maintains stability under complex dynamics, severe communication delays, and sensor noise, reducing communication traffic by over 90% and 84% compared with periodic and static event-triggered benchmarks, respectively.

title: Online Feasible Region Characterization of Aggregated DERs via Incremental Projection
abstract: Performing fast and accurate feasible region characterization (FRC) for aggregated distributed energy resources (DERs) is essential for real-time operational dispatching. Affected by the temporal coupling and the uncertainty associated with DERs, the aggregated feasible regions exhibit high-dimensional coupling and strong stochasticity. However, existing methods cannot quickly perform accurate FRC of the entire operational domain, resulting in preventing real-time updating of FRC based on rolling forecasts of uncertain sources and loads. To this end, an incremental projection-based online full-time-domain FRC method is proposed in this paper, which requires only a local projection of the forecasts to achieve fast and accurate FRC. First, the reversible decoupling equivalent reformulation is developed to decompose the original high-dimensional FRC into several sliced low-dimensional FRCs, while the temporal coupling feature is retained. Then, to shorten the computation time, a universal incremental projection paradigm is constructed, in which the whole FRC is quickly updated by replacing local projections in the complete FRC results obtained offline. Statistical analysis validates that the proposed method can reduce the computation time in the order of 0.55% compared to that of the existing techniques without losing accuracy.

title: Secure State Estimation Design for Power Converter Dominated AC Microgrids
abstract: With the rapid expansion of smart devices and the digitalization of microgrids, cyber-attacks have become an increasing concern, posing significant threats to the security and stability of microgrids. Traditional observer-based state estimation methods provide a robust approach to mitigating the impact of cyber-attacks. However, they often suffer from estimation errors when dealing with both unknown disturbances, such as voltage couplings and load conditions, and faulty measurements caused by adversarial sensor attacks. To overcome this challenge, this paper contributes a new secure state estimation method by proposing a novel design of unknown input observers (UIOs) to ensure accurate estimation of microgrid voltages and currents under these adverse conditions. First, the estimation inaccuracy problem is analyzed, followed by a detailed design of the proposed estimation methods. A feasibility study is conducted to validate the practicality of the proposed approach. Furthermore, the stability of the UIO-integrated microgrid control system is evaluated. The effectiveness of the proposed estimation approach is verified through hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) testing on a dSPACE-based platform under various attack scenarios.

title: Decision-Focused Continual Learning for Seaport Power--Logistics Scheduling: Generalization Across Varying Tasks
abstract: Power–logistics scheduling in modern seaports typically follows a predict-then-optimize pipeline. To enhance the decision quality of predictions, decision-focused learning has been proposed, which aligns the training of forecasting models with downstream decision outcomes. However, this end-to-end design inherently restricts the value of forecasting models to a specific task structure and therefore generalizes poorly to evolving tasks induced by varying vessel arrivals. We address this gap with a decision-focused continual learning framework that adapts online to a stream of scheduling tasks. Specifically, we introduce Fisher-information-based regularization to enhance cross-task generalization by preserving parameters critical to prior tasks. A differentiable convex surrogate is also developed to stabilize gradient backpropagation. The proposed approach enables learning a decision-aligned forecasting model across a varying task stream with sustainable long-term computational and memory requirements. Experiments calibrated to Jurong Port show improved decision performance and cross-task generalization over existing methods, together with reduced computational cost and a bounded memory footprint.

title: A Genetic-Reinforcement Learning Algorithm Based Fuzzy Distributed Frequency Regulation Strategy With Virtual Power Plant Under PMU Missing Data
abstract: This paper investigates the frequency regulation problem on power system with virtual power plant (VPP) under phasor measurement unit (PMU) missing data. First, the distributed load frequency control (LFC) incorporating VPP is established, in which a unified dynamic model based on VPP is introduced with the consideration of PMU missing data. Then, a genetic-reinforcement learning algorithm is developed to optimize the power output of various frequency regulation resources. Furthermore, a fuzzy dynamic event-triggered mechanism (FDETM) is proposed to achieve the balance between bandwidth resource utilization and frequency regulation performance. Finally, theoretical analysis is conducted using Lyapunov theory. Sufficient conditions for ensuring the system stability are derived. Evaluations on IEEE 9-bus test system in MATLAB/Simulink and IEEE 39-bus test system on hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) experiment platform demonstrate the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed strategy.

title: Adaptive Liquid Time-Constant Equivalent Dynamic Model With Transfer Learning for Active Distribution Networks With Grid-Forming IBRs
abstract: Active distribution networks (ADNs) integrating grid-forming and grid-following inverter-based resources (IBRs) introduce complex dynamics and demand accurate, practical data-driven models for integrated transmission-distribution system analysis and control. Existing models, however, require extensive data and lack versatility across diverse ADN operating conditions and configurations. To address these limitations, this paper leverages recent advances in machine learning and presents a data-driven liquid-time-constant (LTC) equivalent dynamic model for ADNs. The LTC architecture enables an enhanced representation of the complex temporal dynamics of ADNs with IBRs, including their source and control dynamics. Further, the proposed model integrates transfer learning (TL) to enable knowledge transfer across operational scenarios and improve prediction robustness and accuracy in data-scarce, realistic ADNs. A modified version of the CIGRE ADN benchmark, interconnected with the WSCC 9-bus transmission system, is used for extensive comparative studies. Compared with long short-term memory, nonlinear autoregressive exogenous, and Kolmogorov–Arnold network models, the proposed model demonstrated robustness, accuracy, low latency, low memory consumption, and generalization across a wide range of operating conditions, particularly during severe disturbances such as short-circuit faults and under limited-data conditions. Furthermore, the proposed LTC model exhibited improved resilience under unseen disturbances, out-of-distribution operating scenarios, and variations in both system parameters and modeling assumptions. Moreover, testing on ADNs with different configurations, such as the CIGRE ADN and modified IEEE 33-bus and IEEE 69-bus ADNs, shows that the integrated LTC–TL framework provides superior cross-topology generalization, enabling effective knowledge transfer when fine-tuned using limited target-domain datasets from such heterogeneous benchmarks.

title: Multi-Frequency Injection-Based Wideband Signal Measurement Method and Its Application in Grid-Connected Inverter
abstract: Wideband impedance characteristics play an essential role in renewable energy grid-connected stability analysis, and multi-frequency injection based wideband signal measurement is an effective method to extract impedance characteristics quickly. However, due to the spectral leakage and low frequency resolution, existing measurement methods such as fast Fourier transform (FFT) suffer from poor measurement accuracy under multi-frequency conditions. To tackle this issue, a wideband measurement method is proposed to extract grid-inverter impedance characteristics from the time-domain perspective. First, the concept of deterministic components in impedance measurement is introduced, and the impedance measurement is regarded as deterministic components measurement. Then, a high-precision deterministic components measurement method is proposed. By approximating the fundamental frequency through a first polynomial fitting and then solving the deterministic components through a second polynomial fitting, the deterministic components can be accurately extracted in the presence of fundamental frequency deviation and noise. To validate the performance of the proposed method, simulations and actual measurement experiments are carried out. The results demonstrate that the impedance amplitude errors of the proposed method are less than 1.8 dB, and the phase errors are less than 5.5° under the test conditions, which are significantly lower than those of existing wideband measurement methods.

title: Robust Energy Management of Hybrid Microgrids via a Nonintrusive Load Monitoring Framework With Dual-Task Learning
abstract: Nonintrusive load monitoring (NILM) is a key technology for enhancing the demand-side flexibility of hybrid microgrid systems by enabling appliance-level consumption to be extrapolated from aggregated smart meter data without requiring dedicated sensors for each device. However, existing state-of-the-art NILM approaches based on deep learning neglect the environmental factors representing contextual drivers of energy consumption, and poorly balance the dual objectives of state classification and power estimation during model training. Moreover, existing robust energy management systems are unable to exploit available appliance-level information, particularly under conditions of high renewable energy source (RES) output uncertainties. The present work addresses these issues by proposing a dual-task NILM framework that performs appliance state detection and power consumption estimation jointly, while incorporating the electrical data in smart meters with contextual drivers of energy consumption, including environmental temperature, humidity, and solar radiation, in a multi-source data fusion design. The estimated appliance states and corresponding power consumption values are then embedded into a robust optimization framework for scheduling distributed resources and demand-side flexibility under RES output uncertainties. The superiority of the proposed NILM-based disaggregation and robust energy management approaches is demonstrated in comparison with state-of-the-art benchmark approaches based on the results of case studies using real-world data.

title: Multi-Charging Station Pricing Strategy for Real-Time Congestion Management in Coupled Traffic-Power Networks
abstract: In high-density cities, coordinating charging station (CS) real-time pricing to mitigate traffic congestion is considered a promising approach. However, the increasing complexity of transportation systems and multi-player dynamic interactions limit the effectiveness of existing pricing strategies in real-time congestion management. To address these, a real-time coordinated pricing framework for multiple CSs in coupled traffic-power networks based on Simulation of Urban MObility (SUMO) simulation is proposed in this paper. First, based on the established CS selection model for EVs, SUMO is utilized to simulate the real-time vehicle and road conditions of the transportation system under given charging prices, providing feedback on charging demand as well as individual and global traffic congestion costs. Next, an Adversarial Diverse Ensemble (ADE) surrogate-based traffic state prediction model is developed to overcome the time-intensive nature of SUMO and integrate it into the multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) framework. Then, a Graph Attention Network-based bi-level multi-agent Soft Actor-Critic (GAT-BLMASAC) algorithm is proposed to solve the coordinated pricing problem in a bi-level architecture, where the upper level optimizes bidding strategies of generation companies (GenCos) as price-makers and the lower level coordinates pricing among CSs as price-takers. Finally, simulations on a real-world Hong Kong transport network demonstrate that the pricing strategies derived from the proposed framework significantly mitigate traffic congestion while enhancing the total profit of CSs. The proposed algorithm exhibits robust convergence in the multi-leader-multi-follower game, offering a scalable solution for coordinated CS pricing in high-density urban settings.

title: Fractional-Order Distributed Current Sharing Control for Power-Coupled Multi-Bus DC Microgrids: A Hierarchical Consensus Approach
abstract: Although the primary fractional-order PI controller, which can improve dynamic response features, has been widely applied in DC microgrids, the relative distributed secondary control has not been proposed to achieve accurate current sharing for multi-bus DC microgrids with power coupling items and composite load generalized disturbances (including constant power/current loads). Thus, this paper introduces a fractional-order distributed secondary control (FODSC) strategy specifically designed for such multi-bus DC microgrids. Firstly, the standard fractional-order multi-agent state-space function model is built, including a primary fractional-order PI controller, a power coupling item, and so on. This standard model is an important foundation for hierarchical control design. Secondly, the state compensator is designed to solve the heterogeneous problem, which is caused by different energy resource rated capacity, RLC filter, and so on. Furthermore, the fractional-order distributed secondary control strategy is proposed to achieve accurate current sharing for multi-bus DC microgrids with power coupling items, effectively overcoming the negative damping effect induced by constant power loads. Meanwhile, the stability proof of the proposed control strategy is provided. Furthermore, a cyber-physical resilient mechanism is integrated to enable plug-and-play operations and system fault tolerance. Finally, simulation and Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) experimental results are presented to demonstrate the effectiveness and practical implementability of the proposed strategy in achieving accurate current sharing.

title: Linear-Complexity Unified Defense Against Deception Attacks in Distributed Economic Dispatch Using Cryptography and Machine Learning
abstract: Deception attacks, including false data injection, replay, and Byzantine manipulation, can corrupt broadcast price signals in distributed economic dispatch (DED), breaking fairness and increasing generation costs while remaining stealthy. Existing defenses are often attack-specific and rely on inter-supplier cross-verification, incurring <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\mathcal {O}(n^{2})$ </tex-math></inline-formula> communication overhead, and many provide probabilistic detection that can cause false alarms or missed attacks. To deterministically detect multiple deception attacks with <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\mathcal {O}(n)$ </tex-math></inline-formula> complexity, this paper proposes a unified security layer for DED based on threshold Schnorr signatures, ensuring data integrity, freshness, and global consistency of price broadcasts. Upon detection, the framework triggers a machine-learning-based robust post-attack recovery mechanism that estimates the true marginal price from historical demand–price correlations, enabling suppliers to continue near-optimal updates. Supplier privacy is preserved via lightweight pairwise masking that reveals only aggregate supply without sacrificing accuracy. The proposed scheme tolerates up to <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\lfloor (n-1)/3 \rfloor $ </tex-math></inline-formula> malicious suppliers among <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$n$ </tex-math></inline-formula>. Experiments on the IEEE 14-bus system quantify efficiency loss under representative attacks. Large-scale studies on the IEEE 118-bus system demonstrate that Byzantine manipulation can increase the system cost by up to 47%. In contrast, the proposed scheme limits the resulting efficiency loss to 0.3% by leveraging an offline-trained LightGBM predictor that achieves an <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$R^{2}$ </tex-math></inline-formula> score of 0.985 on the test set.

title: A Smoothing Pseudo-Labeling Framework for FDIA Detection Under Large Load Integration
abstract: Real-world cyber intrusions, such as the 2022 Ukraine power-grid attack, have underscored the vulnerability of modern smart grid operation. While deep learning has exhibited promise in false data injection attack (FDIA) detection, its reliability is often compromised by evolving grid conditions, especially those driven by large load integration. Such substantial load variations alter the statistical characteristics of operational patterns, rendering existing FDIA detectors ineffective. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a Smoothing Pseudo-Labeling (SPL) framework. SPL utilizes a fine-tuning mechanism to efficiently transfer diagnostic knowledge from historical operational patterns to new scenarios. Specifically, the framework integrates pseudo-labeling to leverage unlabeled data from new environments, while applying label smoothing regularization on labeled samples to mitigate overfitting and enhance robustness against noisy predictions. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework adapts effectively to dynamic grid environments. SPL achieves detection performance comparable to state-of-the-art benchmarks while requiring only 10% of the labeled data and 42.62% of the training time.

title: Two-Stage Privacy-Preserving Collaborative Forecasting for Wind Generation With Defense Against Malicious Eavesdroppers and Saboteurs
abstract: Wind power generation point forecasting involves trade-offs among accuracy, privacy, attack resilience, and training efficiency. Individual forecasting (IF) protects data privacy but often suffers from limited accuracy, whereas collaborative forecasting (CF) exploits cross-farm correlations but may introduce privacy risks, malicious attacks, and high training costs. To address these challenges, this paper proposes an efficient two-stage privacy-preserving CF framework. In Stage 1, each wind farm trains an IF model independently and in parallel. In Stage 2, all farms collaboratively train a collaborative fine-tuning (CFT) model to learn IF residuals, improving forecasting accuracy while reducing the collaborative training burden. Considering two types of malicious attackers in information interaction, namely eavesdroppers and saboteurs, targeted defense mechanisms are further designed. For eavesdroppers, secure multi-party computation is embedded into the CFT process, enabling both forward and backward propagation to be performed over secret shares and preventing privacy leakage. For saboteurs, dropout-embedded self-attention and quantile regression are incorporated to mitigate the impact of tampered collaborative information and constrain abnormal residual corrections. Case studies on real-world data from 10 wind farms in Jiangsu Province, China, and the public GEFCom2014 dataset show that the proposed method achieves higher accuracy and lower collaborative training cost than federated-learning-based CF. Sensitivity analyses further reveal the effects of key defense-related parameters, providing practical guidance for parameter tuning under different security requirements.

title: Vulnerability of Time-Series AI Detectors to Physics-Informed Poisoning Attacks
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has been extensively integrated into smart grids to enhance anomaly detection, with time-series AI detectors such as Long Short-Term Memory Autoencoders (LSTM-AE) and Convolutional Autoencoders (Conv-AE) emerging as pivotal technologies for handling sequential data and intricate temporal dependencies. However, this integration exposes critical infrastructure to novel security vulnerabilities, particularly during the model training phase. This paper investigates an underexplored threat: black-box training-data poisoning attacks on time-series AI detectors in power systems. Unlike gradient-based test-time evasion attacks such as the Fast Gradient Sign Method and Carlini & Wagner, our attack is formulated as a black-box training-data corruption framework that poisons archived load records before detector training. We introduce a physics-informed attack framework that leverages Stochastic Differential Equations (SDEs) to generate physically plausible poisoned load records. The methodology encompasses empirical SDE parameter extraction, template-based synthetic load generation with daily drift compensation, and its integration into an Automatic Generation Control (AGC) system to systematically contaminate the training dataset. Simulation results reveal that time-series AI detectors trained on this tainted data exhibit profound detection failures, misclassifying severe anomalies—such as system frequency drops below 49.5 Hz—as normal operations, thereby underscoring a critical vulnerability in AI-enabled power systems and the urgent need for defenses against such physics-constrained adversarial threats.

title: Weather-Aware Feeder Fault Prediction Based on Graph Learning With Synthetic Rare Event Generation
abstract: The increasing frequency and intensity of extreme weather events have significantly challenged the reliability of power distribution systems. Accurate prediction of weather-related feeder fault states under such conditions is hindered by two fundamental issues: 1) the mismatch between the Euclidean assumptions of traditional machine learning and the inherently graph-structured nature of distribution feeders, and 2) the severe class imbalance caused by the rarity of weather-related fault data. To overcome these challenges, this paper proposes a novel framework that integrates a graph convolutional network (GCN) with a conditional generative adversarial network (cGAN). The proposed GCN-cGAN framework captures topological dependencies of feeders while synthesizing realistic rare fault events under extreme weather scenarios. A graph attention-based model is further developed for feeder fault prediction, leveraging both real and synthetic data samples. Extensive experiments on real distribution topology and meteorological data show consistent gains under multiple evaluation scenarios, including strong wind, heavy rainfall, and their combination, with marked robustness to class imbalance. Under the present prediction setting, compared with conventional and state-of-the-art baselines, Recall improves by about 28 percent and F1-score by about 21 percent.

title: Two-Stage Active Distribution Network Voltage Control via LLM-RL Collaboration: A Hybrid Knowledge-Data-Driven Approach
