abstract: The growing integration of distributed photovoltaics (PVs) into active distribution networks (ADNs) has exacerbated operational challenges, making it imperative to coordinate diverse equipment to mitigate voltage violations and enhance power quality. Although existing data-driven approaches have demonstrated effectiveness in the voltage control problem, they often require extensive trial-and-error exploration and struggle to incorporate heterogeneous information, such as day-ahead forecasts, semantic-based grid codes, and historical records. Considering the operational scenarios and requirements in real-world ADNs, in this paper, we propose a hybrid knowledge-data-driven approach that leverages dynamic collaboration between a large language model (LLM) agent and a reinforcement learning (RL) agent to achieve two-stage voltage control. In the day-ahead stage, the LLM agent receives coarse region-level forecasts and generates scheduling strategies for on-load tap changer (OLTC) and shunt capacitors (SCs) to regulate the overall voltage profile. Then in the intra-day stage, based on real-time node-level measurements, the RL agent refines terminal voltages by deriving reactive power generation strategies for PV inverters. On top of the LLM-RL collaboration framework, we further propose a self-evolution mechanism for the LLM agent and a pretrain-finetune pipeline for the RL agent, effectively enhancing and coordinating the policies for both agents. The proposed approach not only aligns more closely with practical operational characteristics but also effectively combines the complementary advantages of the LLM agent and the RL agent, significantly improving overall training efficiency and voltage control performance. Comprehensive comparisons and ablation studies demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

title: Trustworthy Reinforcement Learning for Renewable Base Energy Management Against Communication Failures
abstract: Renewable energy integration introduces volatility, posing significant challenges to power systems energy management. Conventional methods struggle to handle the volatility relying on high-fidelity models. Recently, reinforcement learning (RL) offers an alternative by learning control policies based on environment interaction. However, communication failures and MW-scale renewable volatility cause delayed state perception and cascaded constraint violations, threatening both system reliability and economic efficiency, and limiting RL deployment. We formulate a communication-failure-tolerant DRL (CFT-DRL) framework that considers the grid-consistent belief state and physically operational envelopes simultaneously. A state belief estimation module is designed to alleviate state perception bias caused by communication failures. An operational-envelope-embedded mechanism is developed to incorporate operational envelopes into policy updates, complemented by a security execution layer to ensure strict constraint satisfaction. Considering the efficient learning and deployment feasibility, we align the policy exploration with physical state transitions. Comparative studies demonstrate superior robustness, operational feasibility, and readiness for practical deployment of the proposed method.

title: Hierarchical Operation of Large-Scale Multi-Energy Systems With Real-Time V2G and Heat Pump Control
abstract: In this paper, we present a real-time control strategy for large-scale Multi-Energy Systems (MES) with coupled electrical, thermal, and gas networks. A novel hierarchical operator-to-operator framework is proposed to coordinate flexible resources, such as Electric Vehicles (EVs) in Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) mode and Heat Pumps (HPs), to mitigate operational challenges in MES. Accounting for V2G peculiarities, including four-quadrant operation, EV driver behaviour, and V2G agreements, we show how EVs can function as flexible storage units that provide ancillary services such as voltage regulation, loss reduction, and cost minimization. Moreover, HPs equipped with thermal storage cooperate with V2G to enhance flexibility and improve energy efficiency across coupled sectors. A realistic large-scale MES based on our research center infrastructure (Forschungszentrum Jülich) is used for validation. Results indicate that the hierarchical framework enables scalable real-time coordination of numerous EVs and HPs under practical constraints, confirming its suitability for large-scale MES.

title: Real-Time Measurement of Transition Resistance and Full-Time Fault Feeder Selection for Random Arc-Fault in Active Distribution Networks
abstract: Single-phase-to-ground fault occurs frequently in active distribution network, often accompanied by nonlinear arc, and the fault development trend changes instantaneously and randomly. However, the existing fault detection methods for stable faults or specific arc faults are difficult to work in practical fault conditions. To achieve real-time tracking of the fault development trend, precise identification of fault types, and reliable selection of fault feeder for random faults occurring in complex and diverse environments, a novel method for real-time measurement of transition resistance and full-time fault feeder selection is proposed in this paper. Firstly, an equivalent circuit diagram of the active distribution network is established considering the parameter asymmetry and damping ratio, to acquire the current flowing through the transition resistance and the voltage across it in real time. Subsequently, the transition resistances of various types of faults are measured in real time based on Ohm’s law, and the stability, periodicity and mutation characteristics of the measured transition resistance are utilized to accurately identify the fault type and track its development trend. Finally, the zero-sequence current is decomposed to eliminate, as much as possible, components irrelevant to fault feeder selection. This process ensures that the characteristic waveforms of the fault feeder and normal feeders remain in opposite phases throughout the entire time period, thereby preventing selection failures caused by the loss of critical transient information. Simulation and 10kV experimental platform prove the feasibility of the proposed methods.

title: Robust Unknown Input Observer-Based Estimation and Mitigation Against Sensor Spoofing Attacks in Cyber-Physical Microgrids
abstract: Microgrids are increasingly dependent on real-time sensing and network communication for the monitoring and control of distributed energy resources (DERs), exposing them to numerous cyber attacks such as sensor spoofing. In such attacks, additive biases are injected into sensor measurements without directly spoofing the communication network and control logic. Conventional observer-based bias estimation methods face several challenges. They typically rely on accurate system models, and their estimation performance deteriorates in the presence of system uncertainties, including parameter uncertainties, process and measurement noise, and unknown inputs. These factors make sensor spoofing-induced biases difficult to distinguish from normal state variations, causing interaction between sensor biases and system uncertainties and leading to degraded control performance in practical microgrid operation. To overcome these limitations, this paper proposes a Robust Unknown Input Observer (RUIO) for the accurate estimation of sensor spoofing-induced biases in the presence of various system uncertainties. The sensor bias is modeled as an augmented state, and the observer gain is synthesized using Linear Matrix Inequality (LMI) optimization under an ${\mathcal {H}}_{\infty } $ performance criterion to ensure robustness against system uncertainties. Given the structural observability limitation of the Unknown Input Observer (UIO) formulation, which prevents simultaneous estimation of independent current and voltage sensor biases, an event-triggered bias estimation and mitigation framework is designed to counter any single sensor spoofing attack. The dual-RUIO scheme is switched adaptively based on the current-sharing error after mitigation, with an appropriate holding interval incorporated to ensure stable operation. The effectiveness of the proposed RUIO-based framework is validated through extensive experiments on a cyber-physical microgrid testbed. Comparative evaluations against conventional state estimation methods demonstrate improved estimation accuracy and mitigation performance.

title: Learning-Augmented Mixed-Integer Reformulation for Dynamic Traffic and Energy Assignment in Spatio-Temporal V2G Coordination
abstract: The increasing integration of electric vehicles (EVs) enables grid services through spatio-temporal vehicle-to-grid (V2G) technology. While prior studies have explored dynamic traffic assignment (DTA) for EV charging management, most existing DTA formulations treat charging and discharging power as exogenous or fixed parameters, limiting V2G flexibility utilization and coordination. This work proposes a learning-augmented mixed-integer reformulation for dynamic traffic and energy assignment (DTEA) that co-optimizes EV traffic flows and continuous (dis)charging power. Specifically, to address the nonlinear flow-power coupling terms, we develop a structure-preserving constraint learning-based method that replicates only the nonlinear coupling terms while retaining the operational constraints. The trained neural networks (NNs) are embedded into the optimization model through tractable mixed-integer reformulations, and data-driven local trust-region restrictions are introduced to mitigate extrapolation risk and improve solution reliability. Case studies demonstrate the effectiveness, scalability, and robustness of the proposed solution method.

title: FedAvgIm: Federated Learning for Multi-Site Impedance Identification of Inverter-Based Resources
abstract: With the increasing integration of inverter-based resources (IBRs) into power systems, assessing small-signal interaction stability has become essential. Impedance/admittance models enable frequency-domain characterization of IBR dynamics without requiring access to proprietary internal control details, but measurement-based identification is time-consuming and must be repeated across operating points. This paper proposes FedAvgIm, a privacy-aware federated-learning framework for multi-site dq-admittance identification under severe local data scarcity and raw-data-locality constraints. Each IBR site trains a local feed-forward neural network using a small set of operating-point–frequency samples, while only model parameters are shared with a cloud aggregator that performs sample-size-weighted FedAvg to update a global model and broadcast it back to all sites. To demonstrate effectiveness, EMT measurement-based admittance datasets are constructed for nine grid-following IBRs with different parameters, architectures, measurement-noise levels, and non-IID settings, where each client has only 40–390 training samples. Results show that FedAvgIm achieves performance close to centralized training and consistently outperforms local-only learning and raw-data-locality-preserving transfer-learning baselines. Additional studies show that FedAvgIm maintains stable learning behavior under measurement noise and remains beneficial under moderate non-IID conditions. The estimated dq-admittance models are further applied to generalized Nyquist stability analysis and validated against EMT time-domain simulations under multiple operating points and grid-strength conditions.

title: Physics-Guided Data-Driven Power Flow Modeling for Unbalanced Distribution Feeders Without Phasor Measurements
abstract: Accurate power-flow (PF) modeling in medium-voltage distribution feeders is challenging due to incomplete physical parameters, for which data-driven approaches provide a flexible and effective solution. However, available data are mostly scalar measurements from transformer low-voltage sides without phase angles. In three-phase three-wire (3P3W) feeders, strong inter-phase coupling caused by line mutual impedances and transformer connections further limits the accuracy of purely data-driven models. Although physics-guided methods have demonstrated strong robustness to measurement errors in vector-domain modeling, effective mechanisms for incorporating physical guidance under scalar measurements are still lacking. To address this gap, this paper proposes a physics-guided data-driven scalar PF model. The model establishes equivalent scalar mappings that characterize feeder and transformer coupling, embedding this physical guidance into the data-driven regression process. Case studies demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves high accuracy, robustness, and physical consistency, ensuring reliable PF estimation even under large measurement errors and strong phase-coupling conditions.

title: Autonomous Topology Identification in Distribution Networks Using Smart Meter Data
abstract: This paper proposes a data-driven and autonomous topology identification framework for distribution networks when topology information is unknown. Using only smart-meter measurements and requiring no prior network information or phasor data, the proposed method identifies the network topology via admittance matrix (Ybus) estimation and a two-stage grouping process. To mitigate the accuracy degradation of the conventional Ybus estimation under partial observability, we develop an advanced Ybus estimation method based on singular value decomposition (SVD). For topology identification, Stage 1 performs preliminary grouping in a fully data-driven manner using the proposed optimal k-means++-based clustering on the estimated admittance matrix. Stage 2 autonomously corrects misgrouping by enforcing physical consistency with the measurements and finalizes the resulting topology. The framework is validated on multiple distribution networks. Furthermore, to verify its real-world applicability, unit tests and a hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) implementation are conducted.

title: Physically Consistent Sparse Identification of Nonlinear Dynamics (SINDy) for Microgrid Identification and Real-Time Frequency Control
abstract: This paper proposes PC-SINDYc, a novel framework for the identification and frequency control of microgrids (MGs) with distributed energy resources. By leveraging physics-guided library construction, total least squares regression, and random sample consensus, the regression algorithm of PC-SINDYc robustly identifies the true frequency dynamics of MGs from phasor measurement unit (PMU) data, considering noise, delays, and constraint activations. Based on the identified model, the PC-SINDYc framework further incorporates a model predictive controller (MPC) for real-time frequency control. We prove that, under mild conditions, PC-SINDYc ensures asymptotic stability of the MG. Simulations on 4-bus and 13-bus MGs demonstrate that PC-SINDYc effectively controls MG’s frequency across various disturbances unseen during the offline identification, outperforming PI controllers, conventional SINDYc, and state-of-the-art reinforcement learning methods.

title: Assessment of Sequential Frequency Regulation Potential of Polysilicon Loads Under Weak Observability via Inverse-Optimization
abstract: High renewable penetration has increased the demand for flexible frequency regulation resources in power systems. As an energy-intensive upstream sector of the photovoltaic manufacturing chain, the polysilicon industry has considerable frequency regulation potential. However, its reliable assessment is challenged by weak observability of production states and the lack of a clear sequential response mechanism. This paper proposes a method to assess the sequential frequency regulation potential of polysilicon loads under weak observability based on inverse optimization. First, a state-task-network-based process model is developed to describe the coupling between production states and electricity consumption. Then, an inverse-optimization-based state estimation model is constructed, in which typical disturbance scenarios are incorporated to enhance robustness. Finally, the continuous regulation potential and economic performance over multiple time intervals are evaluated by considering temporal coupling and response aversion costs. Case studies show that the proposed method yields regulation capacity estimates close to the theoretical upper bound under full-information conditions while satisfying production constraints, thereby demonstrating its effectiveness and economic viability.

title: Sensing-Communication-Computing Integrated Resource Allocation for 3D Observability Enhancement of Distribution Grid
abstract: To address poor observability of distribution grid under constrained communications, this paper proposes a three-dimensional (3D) observability enhancement framework under sensing-communication-computing integration. It builds a 3D observability model covering numerical, temporal, and spatial dimensions, which are quantified via dynamic time warping (DTW) sequence similarity, sensed data peak age of information (PAoI), and unobservable extreme event ratios. For sensing, scenarized cascading inter-dependencies between electrical equipment states are leveraged, significantly improving distributed learning convergence while enabling event-driven accurate data sensing. For transmission, the proposed algorithm infers device-server-channel matching preferences via bounded Q-matching, and addresses the externality dilemma caused by co-channel interference coupling with signal to interference plus noise ratio (SINR) bound violation-driven swap operations. For computing, an age of information (AoI)-greedy heuristic mechanism iteratively allocates resources by prioritizing data computing needs of devices with higher AoI proportions. Simulations verify its effectiveness in improving 3D observability, distributed photovoltaic absorption, and economic energy dispatch.

title: Edge AI-Enabled PMU Event Classification With Knowledge Distillation and Federated Learning
abstract: Phasor Measurement Units (PMUs) enable analysis and classification of events and abnormalities in modern power systems. However, in large and geographically dispersed networks, centralizing PMU data streams for sub-second decisions is hindered by cross-regional data-sharing restrictions, multi-layer aggregation, as well as communication delays and jitter. Purely local training at the network edge on the PMU devices themselves can avoid these bottlenecks but lacks exposure to diverse operating conditions, leading to suboptimal models. This tension calls for methods that retain data locality and privacy while sharing knowledge efficiently. To this end, this paper proposes an edge AI framework that integrates knowledge distillation and federated learning, driven by the core requirement of different data-sharing constraints. First, we assume a trusted data center, where we develop a large language model-based teacher model that is fine-tuned on global data and efficiently transfers knowledge into student models trained locally via knowledge distillation. Next, we relax such an assumption and design a fair federated learning framework that exchanges gradient information among edge models while enforcing Pareto-optimal fairness to ensure stable and balanced performance. We also customize a lightweight neural network tailored for on-device deployment. With fewer than 5,000 parameters, the model adopts a compact end-to-end architecture to effectively characterize temporal dynamics and frequency-domain information in PMU time series, thereby achieving both high efficiency and strong representational capability. Experiments conducted on real-world PMU measurements demonstrate the superior performance of our framework, and ablation studies further confirm the unique contributions of each design component.

title: Privacy-Preserving Generation Fraud Detection for Distributed Photovoltaic Systems: A Solar Irradiance-Fused Federated Learning Framework
abstract: The wide adoption of residential photovoltaic (PV) systems introduces new challenges for generation fraud detection (FD). Unlike traditional electricity theft detection, which focuses on electricity consumption-side behavior, PV generation fraud detection (PVG-FD) is complicated by the inherent intermittency and uncertainty of PV generation. The distributed nature of PV systems poses further challenges for centralized PVG-FD approaches due to scalability and privacy concerns. This paper develops a privacy-preserving distributed PVG-FD framework based on federated learning (FL). In this framework, a utility company manages multiple household communities, where each of which is equipped with a local detector. The framework integrates a novel detection model architecture with privacy-preserving global collaboration. Each community’s local model fuses PV generation and weather data via a co-attention mechanism to detect discrepancies critical for PVG-FD. The FL framework enables cross-community collaboration by aggregating model parameters and prototypes, leveraging global knowledge sharing with local refinement while preserving privacy. It also uses prototype alignment to address class imbalance by enhancing fraud sample representation. Extensive experiments on a real-world residential PV dataset validate the effectiveness of the developed method and demonstrate that it outperforms state-of-the-art FL methods across various scenarios. The results also show its scalability across varying community sizes and strong robustness to class imbalance.

title: A Causal-Guided Multimodal Large Language Model for Generalized Power System Time-Series Data Analytics
abstract: Power system time series analytics is critical in understanding the system operation conditions and predicting the future trends. Despite the wide adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools, many AI-based time series analytical models suffer from task-specificity (i.e., one model for one task) and structural rigidity (i.e., the input-output format is fixed), leading to limited model performance and resource waste. In this paper, we propose a Causal-Guided Multimodal Large Language Model (CM-LLM) that can solve heterogeneous power system time-series analysis tasks. First, we introduce a physics-statistics combined causal discovery mechanism to capture the causal relationship, which is represented by a graph, among power system variables. Second, we propose a multimodal data preprocessing framework that can encode and fuse text, graph and time series to enhance the model performance. Last, we formulate a generic “mask-and-reconstruct” paradigm and design a dynamic input-output padding mechanism to enable CM-LLM to adapt to heterogeneous time-series analysis tasks with varying sample lengths. Simulation results based on open-source LLM Qwen and real-world datasets demonstrate that, after simple fine-tuning, the proposed CM-LLM can achieve satisfying accuracy and efficiency on three heterogeneous time-series analytics tasks: missing data imputation, forecasting and super resolution.

title: A Two-Layer Identification Method for the Transformer-Feeder-Phase Topology of Low-Voltage Distribution Networks Considering Data Incompleteness
abstract: Accurate topology identification for low-voltage distribution networks (LVDN) is fundamental to achieving precise state estimation and effective system control, but existing methods face challenges such as sensitivity to missing data and high dependence to detection equipment. To address these issues, a two-layer identification method for the transformer-feeder-phase topology of LVDN considering voltage data incompleteness is proposed. First, the clustering method combining Newton-Raphson-based optimizer and Gaussian mixture model (NRBO-GMM) is proposed, which integrates Newton-Raphson gradient optimization and intelligent search mechanism to realize high-precision clustering of user voltage data; second, the multiple time scale adaptive weight allocation strategy for single-day topology identification result is constructed, and the clustering results of different scales are dynamically fused by XGBoost to reduce the instability caused by the missing data and single-day identification error; next, based on the phase identification results from the upper layer, the hierarchical user-feeder identification method based on Jenks natural breaks (JNB) and mean absolute error (MAE) minimization is proposed to gradually analyze the feeder attribution of users. Case studies using voltage data from China is performed, and simulation results show that the method can achieve 100% phase identification accuracy with voltage data that only requires a maximum scale of 6 days and an average data missing rate of 42.93%, and that the accuracy of hierarchical user-feeder relationship identification using 10 days of data with a 41.79% missing rate is more than 95%, and reaches 100% for 26 days and remains at this level thereafter. Additionally, the effectiveness and portability of the proposed method between different distribution networks is validated. Thus, the proposed method provides a high-precision and low data requirement topology identification basis for the digital operation and maintenance of LVDN.

title: Unsupervised Lightweight Transfer Learning for Edge Non-Intrusive Load Monitoring
abstract: Non-intrusive load monitoring (NILM) is crucial for residential real-time energy management as it provides appliance-level consumption insights. Deploying NILM at the edge enables immediate feedback and preserves user privacy by processing data locally. While deep learning has significantly advanced NILM, its direct deployment on the edge faces major hurdles. The deep learning models are often too large to be applied to resource-constrained hardware. In addition, their performance may degrade substantially for a new household due to cross-household domain shifts. To overcome these two obstacles, this paper presents a novel lightweight transfer learning framework consisting of two main phases: dynamic network compression (DNC) and lightweight cross-domain transfer (LCT). DNC enables the progressive shrinking training of an elastic supernet in the cloud, which can be flexibly compressed into compact subnets tailored to the memory constraints of various edge devices without retraining. LCT enables efficient fine-tuning of deployed subnets at the edge in an unsupervised manner, adapting them to locally unlabeled cross-domain data by only updating lightweight residual modules. Experiments on a hardware testbed demonstrate that the proposed framework significantly outperforms existing methods in both disaggregation accuracy and memory efficiency, demonstrating its capability to deliver high-performance NILM on various edge devices.

title: Vision of Future Smart Control Center: Fusion of Large Language Models and Power System Intelligent Computing
abstract: The high stochasticity of renewable dominated power grids demands advanced dispatch strategies. However, the disparity between flexible operator intent and rigid legacy tools hinders resilient system operation. To address this challenge,this paper proposes a future smart control center architecture that fuses Large Language Models (LLMs) with Power System Intelligent Computing (PSIC). In this architecture, the LLM functions as the cognitive core for intent understanding, workflow orchestration, and causal reasoning. Concurrently, PSIC executes physical simulations and data-driven optimization tasks decomposed by the LLM. This integration creates a cognitive decision-making process where the adaptive decision-making capability enabled by LLM is rigorously bounded and verified by physical laws. Consequently, the architecture enables next generation human-machine collaborative dispatch, advancing grid operations from automation toward true intelligence and self-evolution.

title: A Novel Synchrophasor Post-Processing Method for Uploading in Distribution Networks Based on Sparse Decomposition
abstract: The large-scale integration of distributed power generations and other power electronic devices into the power grid introduces new challenges for the control and dispatching of distribution networks. Synchrophasor measurements can provide real-time data to meet control requirements. However, the widespread adoption of synchrophasor measurement technology in distribution networks is limited due to several factors such as communication constraints and deployment costs. To address these challenges, this paper proposes an optimized sparse decomposition method for synchrophasor uploading, aimed at characterizing slow dynamic processes with a lower reporting rate. First, an improved Gabor overcomplete dictionary is designed to better capture both the periodicity and abrupt changes in signals within distribution networks. Then, to more efficiently match the optimal atom, the matching pursuit process is enhanced using a Modified Sine-Cosine Algorithm (MSCA). This enhancement is achieved through the optimized initialization of candidate solutions and the application of nonlinear adjustments to control parameters, resulting in improved decomposition efficiency and reconstruction accuracy. Furthermore, the proposed method is implemented on Field Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGA) to enhance the execution parallelism of the algorithm, laying the groundwork for future development of low-cost custom chips suitable for widespread deployment in distribution networks. Experimental evaluations demonstrate that the proposed method can process 100 frames of synchrophasor data within 0.1 seconds, reducing the data volume by over 87% compared to uncompressed transmission. Moreover, it consistently delivers a compression ratio at least 1.5 times higher than benchmark methods across varying data volumes.

title: Carbon-Aware V2G Coordination in PV-Rich Distribution Systems via Weather-Incorporated Two-Stage Graph Reinforcement Learning and Data Distillation
abstract: The increasing penetration of photovoltaic (PV) generation introduces significant volatility and PV-load temporal mismatch into power distribution systems, necessitating advanced strategies to maintain efficient and sustainable operation. While vehicle-to-grid (V2G) technology presents a promising solution by leveraging electric vehicle (EV) fleets as distributed energy storage, coordinating a large fleet of EVs for PV-rich distribution systems remains a complex, high-dimensional problem. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a novel weather-incorporated two-stage graph reinforcement learning approach based on data distillation for carbon-aware V2G coordination. In the first stage, stochastic operational data, including PV generation and load profiles, are distilled according to weather and day types to simplify data patterns. The resulting distilled profiles are then used to pre-train a guidance policy. At the second stage, the pre-trained guidance policy facilitates more effective policy learning for the refined policy by providing guidance actions, enabling it to efficiently handle stochasticity in the original operational data and thereby improving overall learning performance. To further enhance the adaptability of V2G coordination, we design a hierarchical graph neural network (HGNN) that learns spatiotemporal correlations involved in the V2G coordination problem and effectively adapts to changes in system configuration, such as the addition or removal of charging stations, without requiring retraining. Evaluations are conducted on a modified PV-rich IEEE 33-bus system incorporating multiple charging stations, demonstrating its suitability for practical deployment in PV-rich distribution systems.

title: Multi-Timescale Transmission-Distribution Coordination Under Decision-Dependent Uncertainty for Enhancing Economic Performance and Operational Reliability
abstract: Coordinated operation between the transmission network (TN) and distribution networks (DNs) is essential to accommodate the high penetration of distributed photovoltaic (PV). Two gaps remain in TN-DN coordination regarding multi-timescale scheduling and decision-dependent uncertainty (DDU) management. This paper proposes a multi-timescale TN-DN coordinated operation framework, which together provides DDU-aware uncertainty modeling and algorithm design. First, the framework architecture is presented, which includes a day-ahead stage at an hourly resolution and an intra-day stage at a 15-minute resolution. Then, the optimal day-ahead TN-DN coordinated scheduling strategy is developed, which includes day-ahead operation and hourly TN-DN power exchanges. Herein, an improved consensus alternating direction method of multipliers (C-ADMM) is proposed to accelerate the convergence of the multi-timescale TN-DN coordinated operation framework. Finally, the intra-day TN-DN scheduling model is formulated, in which a chance-constrained optimization is adopted to capture DDU characteristics for DNs. The chance constraints are further reformulated as robust constraints via a robust approximation approach to guarantee solution tractability. Case studies verify that the proposed framework increases the accommodation of distributed PV while enhancing the economic performance and operational reliability of ITDS.

title: Generative Autonomous Grid Control: Integrating Decision Transformers With a Two-Stage Safety Stack
abstract: The displacement of synchronous generation by inverter-based resources is accelerating power system frequency dynamics beyond the response capability of conventional automatic generation control. This paper presents Autonomous Grid Generation Control with Decision Transformers, a framework coupling an offline-trained Decision Transformer with a two-stage symbolic safety stack for secondary frequency control. The Decision Transformer learns a conditional dispatch policy from offline supervisory control and data acquisition records via sequence modeling, eliminating online exploration risks. A Constraint Verification Unit provides sub-ten-millisecond algebraic screening using real-time power transfer distribution factors, while an aggregate digital twin performs swing-equation-based dynamic stability certification. Validated on the Northeast Power Coordinating Council 140-bus system under low-inertia conditions, the proposed controller reduces the area control error integral by over 99% relative to tuned automatic generation control, maintains a 59.4 Hz frequency nadir, and achieves inference latency of approximately 10 ms, well within real-time constraints. Comparative evaluation against a linear quadratic regulator baseline and structural analysis against conservative Q-learning demonstrate the advantages of the sequence-modeling formulation. Small-signal eigenvalue analysis characterizes the dominant 1.87 Hz electromechanical mode and confirms that the safety stack maintains stable operation across operating points. By falling back to tuned automatic generation control whenever proposals are rejected, the safety stack bounds worst-case performance to industry-standard levels in simulation.

title: Secure Prespecified-Time Distributed Energy Management via Dual-Layer Privacy-Preserving Mechanism
abstract: This paper investigates the energy management (EM) problem for microgrids in a fast and secure manner. To rapidly obtain the optimal power output combination, a flexible distributed EM algorithm over digraphs is proposed based on a novel prespecified-time convergence lemma, which enables the presetting of convergence time independent of initial states or algorithmic parameters. Considering the privacy protection of incremental costs (ICs), a new dual-layer privacy-preserving mechanism is devised to defend against both internal honest-but-curious (HBC) distributed generators and external eavesdroppers. The first privacy-preserving layer is state decomposition, which operates throughout the entire scheduling horizon. The second privacy-preserving layer is edge-based additive perturbations, which operates during the coordinated scrambling phase. The state decomposition mechanism divides the ICs into two auxiliary variables, and the additive perturbation method can further protect the privacy of these auxiliary variables. Simulation results are provided to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed EM strategy.

title: Joint Robust and Chance-Constrained Optimization for Pre-Disaster Hardening Strategy of Power-Thermal Cyber-Physical Systems
abstract: The integration of large-scale distributed photovoltaics (PVs) introduces significant operational uncertainties in urban power-thermal cyber-physical systems (PTCPS), particularly during typhoon events, which pose severe risks to system safety. Distribution-based models, such as chance constraints, effectively handle PV uncertainties. However, under extreme typhoon events, the scarcity of component fault data limits the availability of distribution knowledge, thereby reducing their effectiveness. To overcome this challenge, a joint robust and chance-constrained optimization (JRCCO) framework for pre-disaster coordinated hardening of PTCPS is proposed. The framework incorporates parameter distribution knowledge and uncertainty sets to minimize safety investment costs. Notably, multi-region sequential fault decision-dependent uncertainty (DDU) sets, designed to operate without requiring distribution knowledge, are introduced alongside chance constraints for PV output. To address the nonlinearity in chance constraints, a linearization method combining chance capacity and Cornish-Fisher series expansion is developed. Moreover, to improve computational efficiency and universality, a modified relaxed column-and-constraint generation with robust cuts (MRCCG-RC) algorithm is developed, which is complemented by acceleration techniques and supported by theoretical proofs. Two PTCPS of different scales are tested, showing that the strategy can reduce hardening costs by 19.15% and load shedding by 41.61%, effectively enhancing the PTCPS’s performance against typhoon disasters.

title: Robust Energy Management for Distributed Energy Resources Using Homothetic Tube-Based Economic Model Predictive Control
abstract: Conventional tube-based model predictive control often suffers from excessive conservatism and sub-optimal economic performance when applied to microgrid energy management due to its reliance on rigid uncertainty bounds. To overcome these limitations, this paper proposes a novel hierarchical homothetic tube-based economic model predictive control (HT-EMPC) framework for the optimal coordination of distributed energy resources (DERs) under uncertainties. By constructing a nested structure of dynamically scaled tubes for both intraday scheduling and real-time control, the proposed approach accurately characterizes uncertainty propagation and significantly reduces operational conservatism by enlarging the feasible region for nominal optimization. The economic efficiency of the coordination is further enhanced through a vertex-based robust objective function, which tractably evaluates operational costs at the extreme points of the homothetic error tubes to ensure robustness against worst-case state deviations. Furthermore, the framework is supported by a rigorous theoretical analysis that provides a formal guarantee of robust state invariance, confirming the system’s recursive feasibility and safety against fast-varying real-time disturbances. Comparative studies on microgrid systems validate that the proposed HT-EMPC strategy achieves a superior balance between adaptive robustness and economic performance compared to both nominal and rigid-tube MPC benchmarks.

title: A Probabilistic Graph Reinforcement Learning for Resilient Service Restoration via Microgrid Formation
abstract: Service restoration in distribution systems after major outages is a complex and time-sensitive task under significant uncertainty and high penetration of distributed energy resources (DERs). Conventional deep reinforcement learning (DRL) methods typically rely on Markov decision processes (MDPs) and Euclidean state representations, limiting their ability to capture stochastic temporal dynamics and network topology. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a probabilistic graph reinforcement learning framework for microgrid formation. The restoration problem is formulated as a semi-Markov decision process (SMDP) to explicitly model stochastic state sojourn times. A Bayesian graph convolutional network is developed to jointly capture spatial dependencies and parameter uncertainty. Building on this, a novel Bayesian graph soft actor-critic (BGSAC) algorithm is proposed, where the entropy regularization coefficient is adaptively adjusted based on uncertainty estimates, enhancing exploration capability and robustness in uncertain environments. Experimental results on the IEEE 123-bus system demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing DRL approaches in convergence stability and final performance. Moreover, compared with optimization-based and heuristic baselines, it achieves comparable restoration effectiveness with substantially reduced decision time, highlighting its suitability for real-time service restoration.

title: A Graph Neural Network With Auxiliary Task Learning for Missing PMU Data Reconstruction
abstract: In wide-area measurement systems (WAMS), phasor measurement unit (PMU) measurement is prone to data missing due to hardware failures, communication delays, and cyber-attacks. Existing data-driven methods are limited by poor adaptability to concept drift in power systems, poor robustness under high missing rates, and reliance on the unrealistic assumption of full system observability. Thus, this paper proposes an auxiliary task learning (ATL) method for reconstructing missing PMU data. First, a K-hop graph neural network (GNN) is proposed to enable direct learning on the subgraph consisting of PMU nodes, overcoming the limitation of the incompletely observable system. Then, an auxiliary learning framework consisting of two complementary graph networks is designed for accurate reconstruction: a spatial-temporal GNN extracts spatial-temporal dependencies from PMU data to reconstruct missing values, and another auxiliary GNN utilizes the low-rank property of PMU data to achieve unsupervised online learning. In this way, the low-rank properties of the PMU data are dynamically leveraged across the architecture to ensure robustness and self-adaptation. Numerical results demonstrate the superior offline and online performance of the proposed method under high missing rates and incomplete observability.

title: Adaptive decision-making model predictive control for multi-objective optimal energy management of hybrid ships
Equilibrium Scheduling Strategy for MSOP via Bayesian Dynamic Segmentation of Complementarity Among LVDNs
abstract: Mobile Soft Open Point (MSOP) technology improves the flexibility and utilization of interconnection resources by enabling mobile deployment across low-voltage distribution networks (LVDNs). However, efficient MSOP scheduling depends on accurately identifying the stage-wise complementarity among interconnectable LVDNs under time-varying source-load conditions. This paper proposes a bi-level equilibrium scheduling framework for MSOP by integrating stage-wise complementarity segmentation with coordinated scheduling optimization. First, a Gaussian mixture model is used to construct the complementary probability matrix among LVDNs, and Bayesian dynamic segmentation is employed to identify statistically stable complementarity stages from its temporal evolution. Then, by incorporating the segmented complementarity stages as stage-wise inputs, a bi-level MSOP scheduling model is developed to coordinate the trade-off between the net benefit of MSOP and the mobile scheduling cost. The scheduling problem is formulated as a Pareto-Nash-equilibrium-based multi-objective coordinated optimization problem. Simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

title: Hybrid Attention-Augmented Self-Interpretable Channel-Grouped Graph Convolutional Network for Robust Distribution Network Fault Diagnosis
abstract: Deep learning (DL)-based methods have illustrated excellent performance in distribution network fault diagnosis. However, the “opaque” nature of DL models hinders grid operators from understanding the decision-making processes of these models, affecting model trustworthiness and robustness in diversified diagnosis applications. This paper proposes a hybrid attention-augmented self-interpretable channel-grouped graph convolutional network (HASIG) for diverse short-circuit fault diagnosis of distribution networks, including binary fault detection, faulted line identification, and fault type classification. A channel-grouped graph convolutional network is proposed to learn features from three-phase voltage and current measurements. We present a hybrid attention that combines global edge attention and channel-grouped attention, which can augment the critical features with faithful and robust interpretations during model training, enabling users to gain insights into the predictive behavior inside the model. These three short-circuit fault diagnosis tasks are collaboratively trained under a multi-task learning architecture with interpretable loss constraints. Experiments were conducted on the IEEE 33-bus, IEEE 33-bus with distributed energy resources, and IEEE 123-bus systems with randomized fault parameters. The results show that HASIG achieves competitive diagnostic performance and good interpretability, and demonstrates strong robustness under noisy and missing-data conditions.

title: Incentive-Compatible Online Pricing of Customer Directrix Load-Based Demand Response for Load Aggregators
abstract: In demand response (DR) programs, load aggregators (LAs) coordinate DR customers to provide flexibility support for the smart grid. However, existing pricing mechanisms often struggle to simultaneously achieve incentive compatibility and operational controllability in retail-side DR. To address this challenge, this paper proposes an incentive compatible online pricing strategy for customer directrix load (CDL)-based DR of LAs. Unlike traditional price-based DR schemes, the proposed approach leverages CDL, which inherently enhances controllability by serving as both the guiding signal and the performance evaluation metric. Within the CDL framework, a DR customer response model and an LA centralized optimization model are established. Under a general discomfort function setting, the centralized response is characterized by a one-dimensional fixed-point equation, based on which a customized incentive compatible pricing strategy is derived to align individual customer responses with the LA’s desired response curve. Furthermore, the widely used quadratic discomfort model is studied as an analytically tractable special case, leading to closed-form response and pricing expressions. An online learning algorithm is then proposed to enable LAs to learn the unobservable discomfort parameters of DR customers from observable response decisions, thereby reducing information exposure and enhancing practical implementation performance. The proposed algorithm is theoretically shown to achieve logarithmic regret with respect to the operating cycle, and a problem-level regret lower bound is further established to show that the minimax cumulative regret of the underlying CDL-based online pricing problem is also logarithmic. Simulation results based on real-world data demonstrate the validity and effectiveness of the proposed method.

title: Contrastive Preference Learning From User Overrides for Personalized Home Energy Management
abstract: Personalizing home energy management systems (HEMSs) to align with dynamic user preferences remains challenging for intelligent energy control. Existing deep reinforcement learning (DRL) approaches typically rely on static reward functions and fixed constraints, limiting their ability to adapt to diverse user behaviors. We propose a framework that leverages user override feedback—instances where users manually correct system decisions—as implicit preference signals. Our method combines contrastive preference learning from pairwise comparisons, context-aware preference embeddings from interaction history, and preference-conditioned DRL policies. This enables the controller to continuously align with personalized preferences without explicit reward engineering. Validation on real-world residential energy data shows that the framework achieves an average override rate of 0.033 across four diverse preference profiles—a 37% reduction over the strongest baseline—while maintaining the lowest user interaction cost (0.394) among all feedback-driven methods. The framework also demonstrates efficient transfer across prototype preferences and generalization to novel behavioral rules.

title: A Data-Driven Probabilistic Harmonic Current Forecasting for Aggregated Harmonic Sources
abstract: With the increasing deployment of non-linear power electronic devices in distribution networks, the issue of excessive harmonics has become increasingly prominent. Accurate analysis and forecasting of harmonic currents are essential to better understand and mitigate harmonic-related problems. Common harmonic sources in power grids include various types of loads and renewable energy generation equipment, such as wind and photovoltaic systems. Accordingly, this paper focuses on forecasting harmonic currents for different types of aggregated harmonic sources. Considering the strong randomness, high time-variability, and coupling characteristics of harmonic currents, a data-driven probabilistic harmonic current forecasting method is proposed. First, the raw data are decomposed into deterministic and stochastic components. Next, a radial basis function autoregressive exponential model is employed to perform point forecasting of the deterministic component, accommodating multiple input factors and simultaneous multi-harmonic outputs while preserving model partial interpretability. Subsequently, the proposed multi-Gaussian fitting method and an improved Markov chain Monte Carlo approach are used for probabilistic forecasting of the stochastic component. Finally, the deterministic and stochastic component predictions are combined to yield the final probabilistic harmonic current forecast. Using actual harmonic measurement data, comparative analyses with multiple intelligent models are conducted to validate the effectiveness and accuracy of the proposed forecasting method. Furthermore, the harmonic current predictions are applied to forward probabilistic harmonic power flows, and corresponding forward and new probabilistic harmonic mitigation measures are proposed, demonstrating practical engineering applicability.

title: A Robust Control Framework for Smooth Operation of PV-Integrated Weak Grids
abstract: The integration of photovoltaic (PV) systems into weak grids poses significant challenges to ensure smooth and stable operation. This paper proposes a robust control framework to ensure the smooth operation of PV-integrated weak grids. The system employs a grid-tied PV generation system sharing a common DC link with a distribution static compensator (DSTATCOM). A hybrid backstepping and barrier function-based sliding mode controller is developed as the core of this framework, serving a dual purpose: it manages the PV generation system for maximum power point tracking and DC-link voltage regulation, while simultaneously controlling the DSTATCOM to mitigate power quality issues. The controller’s robustness is demonstrated through its ability to minimize errors in critical parameters (<inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$V_{pv}$ </tex-math></inline-formula>, <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$V_{dc}$ </tex-math></inline-formula>, <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$I_{d}$ </tex-math></inline-formula>, and <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$I_{q}$ </tex-math></inline-formula>). The framework’s performance is exhaustively evaluated under both linear and nonlinear load conditions via MATLAB/Simulink simulations and validated on a laboratory-scale hardware prototype. A comparative analysis with standard PID and SMC techniques confirms the superiority of the proposed framework, showing significant improvements in total harmonic distortion reduction to 2.18% under linear and 2.46% under nonlinear load conditions, alongside enhanced voltage regulation. The results affirm that the proposed robust control framework is highly effective for maintaining stable, high-quality power in PV-integrated weak grids.

title: From Water Vapor Transmission Rate (WVTR) to Intrinsic Water Vapor Permeability (WVP)
abstract: ABSTRACT Water vapor transmission rate (WVTR) is widely used to assess breathability in skin‐interfaced electronics. In gravimetric wet‐cup tests, however, the measured flux depends on transport through both the membrane and the apparatus. Apparatus resistance can dominate measurements of highly permeable membranes. Evaporation, headspace transport, membrane permeation, and external vapor spreading are modeled as resistances in series under a common chemical‐potential driving force. The apparatus coefficients are calibrated using open‐cup measurements in the same setup, independently of the reference permeability. For poly(dimethylsiloxane) membranes, where membrane resistance dominates, both a literature air‐gap correction and the calibrated model reduce deviations from the reference. For a highly permeable anion‐exchange membrane (AEM), the air‐gap correction becomes unstable. Relative to a dynamic sweep‐cell reference, the calibrated model reduces mean absolute relative deviation from 49.8% for classical conversion to 6.2%. It also provides model‐based criteria for geometry selection and measurement duration, together with a procedure for converting WVTR to water vapor permeability (WVP).

title: Bottom‐Cell Engineering as the Key to Perovskite/CIGS Tandem Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Perovskite/Cu(In,Ga)Se 2 (CIGS) tandem solar cells have emerged as a highly promising thin‐film photovoltaic architecture, combining the exceptional efficiency potential of perovskites with the industrial maturity of CIGS technology. Despite rapid advances in perovskite top cells, overall tandem performance remains fundamentally constrained by the CIGS bottom cell, which critically governs bandgap matching, voltage losses, and interfacial recombination. Here, we provide a comprehensive overview of recent progress in CIGS absorber and interface engineering for tandem applications. We highlight key strategies including Ga‐gradient bandgap engineering, alkali post‐deposition treatment, Ag alloying for low‐temperature growth and bifacial operation, as well as buffer‐layer and intermediate recombination layer optimization. We further discuss how surface morphology and defect chemistry collectively dictate carrier recombination dynamics and interfacial stability in monolithic device architectures. Finally, we outline a roadmap toward the commercialization of perovskite/CIGS tandem photovoltaics. By linking materials‐level engineering with device‐level constraints, this review establishes a unified framework to guide the development of high‐efficiency, scalable, and industrially viable tandem solar technologies.

title: Blending With Insulating Polymers Enables Stable Anti‐Ambipolar Characteristics in n‐Type Organic Mixed‐Conductors for Heterogeneous Spiking Neurons
abstract: ABSTRACT Mammalian neurons exhibit diverse structural and physiological properties: a heterogeneity not present in current neuromorphic systems. Recent advancements have led to bio‐realistic spiking systems which are based on the integration and long‐term operation of organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) with anti‐ambipolar characteristics. However, the library of materials enabling anti‐ambipolarity (AA) is restricted by the lack of stable, fast, and scalable organic mixed ionic and electronic conductors (OMIECs) exhibiting this specific OFF‐ON‐OFF behavior. This complicates mimicking specialized neuron types. Blending semiconducting with insulating polymers is a classic organic and OMIEC electronics strategy to improve device performance and enable tunability, yet unexplored for improving anti‐ambipolar stability in non‐ladder‐type anti‐ambipolar materials. Here, the n‐type OMIEC, P(gNDI‐gT2), is blended with the insulating polymer, PMMA, yielding stable anti‐ambipolar characteristics. The miscibility in solution forms a mechanically stabilizing and ion‐permeable framework in the solid state that considerably reduces swelling‐induced structural damage, thus preventing dramatic failure after the first operation cycles without compromising the conductive polymer's electronic pathways. Modulating the polymer blend ratio enables low‐power, fast‐spiking Hodgkin–Huxley neurons with tunable and programmable dynamics, without optimized device geometries, demonstrating frequency deconvolution and reservoir computing. These two computing primitive building blocks are essential for designing efficient spiking neural networks.

title: Water‐Heat Synergistic Regulation to Optimize Water State and Enhance Thermal Effect in Solar Interfacial Evaporation
abstract: ABSTRACT Solar‐driven interfacial evaporation is a promising solution to the global freshwater shortage. However, current evaporation systems typically suffer from low water management efficiency and poor interfacial thermal effects. This work proposes a strategy to synergistically enhance the heat and mass transport of solar interfacial evaporators by balancing water transport capacity and water activity and reverse heat compensation. A higher proportion of loosely bound intermediate water (IW) with low enthalpy of vaporization is induced by in situ construction of a hydrophilic micron‐to‐submicron hierarchical pore structure within the wood‐based biomass framework, while maintaining its water pumping capacity. Simultaneously, a biomimetic thermal compensation mechanism significantly enhances the thermal effect of the wood‐based biomass evaporation interface (temperature up to 50.7°C). This synergistic design enables a record evaporation rate of 5.12 kg m −2 h −1 in wood‐based evaporators. Furthermore, the vertically distributed hierarchical pore structure and surface polar groups endow it with excellent salt repellency and antifouling capabilities. This reported water‐heat management strategy provides a scalable, low‐cost, and environmentally friendly approach to highly efficient solar interfacial evaporation.

title: Directing solvent reactivity
abstract: Anode-free sodium batteries eliminate excessive sodium on the anode, maximizing cell-level energy density, but are limited by irreversible sodium loss during electroplating–stripping. Now, a low-strain cyclic solvent forms an oligomerized interphase, enabling highly reversible sodium deposition without functional additives or electrode modifications.

title: Stable anode-free sodium batteries enabled by controlled oligomerization
abstract: Anode-free sodium batteries are limited by irreversible sodium loss during cycling. Here the authors introduce a moderate-strain cyclic ether that redirects electrolyte decomposition to form a thin, robust interphase, thereby minimizing sodium consumption and extending cycling stability.

title: Grain boundary engineering using metallomesogen in formamidinium–caesium lead triiodide for stable perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells
abstract: Formamidinium–caesium lead triiodide perovskites show promise in terms of stability, yet their solar cell efficiency remains limited. Li et al. use a metallomesogen with mesophase to stabilize perovskite grain boundaries, improving both the efficiency and stability of perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells.

title: Southeast Asian voices on climate change
abstract: Responding to the increasing risks of climate change in Southeast Asia requires research and effective action that considers the unique challenges of the region. In this Viewpoint, researchers and practitioners from the region share their views on the progress made in understanding and responding to climate change.

title: Breaking symmetry in nanoparticle superlattices via spontaneous valency
abstract: The deformation of flexible ligands in polymer-grafted nanoparticles enables initially isotropic particles to produce effective valency, accessing lattice symmetries with unexpected deviations from densest packing or highest coordination number.

abstract: Non-resonant excitation of WS2 in-plane microcavities generates waveguide exciton–polaritons that carry spin-polarized currents over distances exceeding 90 μm at room temperature and reveal a non-resonantly pumped optical spin Hall effect.

title: Process-intrinsic cellular network for sustained strength–ductility across temperatures in a 3D-printed multi-principal-element alloy
abstract: Laser-based additive manufacturing enables the formation of a self-assembled precipitate cellular network in a multi-principal element alloy, which sustains a yield strength above 1 GPa and a uniform elongation of approximately 20% over a wide temperature range.

title: Trifunctional zirconium catalysis-enabled triple modular synthesis
abstract: Zirconium catalysis has remained largely confined to Lewis acid and redox chemistry, with only isolated examples of photocatalytic C–H activation. Now trifunctional zirconium catalysis enables modular benzylamine synthesis from alkanes, aldehydes and nitriles by integrating photochemical, redox and Lewis acid reactivity.

title: Maternal mental health liveability shaped by composite residential environmental profiles
abstract: In a cohort of 216,000+ pregnant women across China, air pollution and heat were linked to higher risks of prenatal mental distress, while nearby green space was protective. Urban greening could support maternal mental health and healthier cities.

abstract: Applied potential controls charge-transfer kinetics, but thermochemical steps can limit electrocatalytic rates. Now it has been shown that CO-to-methanol conversion shifts from charge-transfer-limited kinetics to adsorption-limited kinetics as overpotential increases, establishing CO adsorption energy as a descriptor of the thermochemical constraint.

abstract: Electrochemical kinetics are shaped by both the thermodynamic driving force and interfacial polarization. title: Set efficiency criteria for access to geological carbon dioxide storage
abstract: Geological CO2 storage sites are critical to achieving climate-relevant carbon sequestration. Efficiency metrics should be used to ensure that limited storage capacity is not used on CO2 from capture projects with high levels of life-cycle carbon emissions.

abstract: Developing and deploying clean technologies to reach net-zero carbon emissions will require more than optimizing individual processes and technologies. System-level thinking is needed to identify trade-offs, handle uncertainty and future scenarios, and support decision-making, as highlighted by articles in a new Collection.

abstract: The use of secondary materials in photovoltaics could reduce resource demand, waste generation and supply-chain risks. This Review benchmarks recycled content use across silicon photovoltaic materials and identifies technical and market barriers to wider adoption.

abstract: A bismuth overlayer reversibly buffers oxidative charge to protect NiCo cathodes. It suppresses metal dissolution and sustains alkaline hydrogen evolution during startup–shutdown and reverse-current cycling under industrially relevant conditions.

title: Rethinking lithium content in inorganic solid-state electrolytes
Control of spin-to-charge conversion by chirality switching of spin texture in a three-dimensional hybrid perovskite
Diagnosis of Mechanisms of Kinetics in Lithium-Rich Manganese-Based Cathode Materials
abstract: Abstract The rate-determining step (RDS), which determines rate capability in lithium-rich manganese-based oxide (LRMO) cathode materials, remains unclear. In this work, we establish a quantitative diagnostic method for the RDS in LRMOs using in-situ electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) and linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) at different states of charge (SOC) and C-rates. From our results, the SOC determines the intrinsic bottleneck of the RDS, while the C-rate drives the transition from single-step to mixed control. Upon discharging to 4.4 V, the RDS is dominated by electron transfer at the interface accompanied by layered-to-spinel phase transition, whereas it is strongly influenced by solid-state diffusion in the bulk with depletion of Li vacancies arising from Jahn–Teller distortion when discharging to 3.0 V. Furthermore, Li+ diffusion, instead of charge transfer, plays a major part in the RDS of LRMOs when the C-rates are increased. These findings establish quantitative criteria for designing future cathode materials.

title: UV Exposure and Durability of Emerging Photovoltaics: Quantifying and Reporting Outdoor UV Doses
abstract: Abstract Ultraviolet (UV) radiation in sunlight is well known to harm components of solar modules, especially those of emerging photovoltaic technologies. Current accelerated UV tests, however, differ in spectral range and by orders of magnitude in intensity and dose. Their usual anchors, IEC 61215-2 preconditioning at 15 kW h m–2 and a fixed UV fraction of AM1.5G, do not represent long-term outdoor exposure. Here, we quantify annual outdoor UV doses (280–400 nm) across the contiguous United States from the National Solar Radiation Database for horizontal, fixed-tilt, and tracked mounting. Spectroradiometer measurements at two sites validate the model. Annual horizontal-plane doses span 72–133 kW h m–2, with a median of nearly 100 kW h m–2, so IEC 61215-2 preconditioning simulates only 1.4–2.5 months of outdoor exposure. Single-axis and dual-axis tracking typically add 10 and 18 kW h m–2, respectively. Finally, we propose reporting the source spectrum and expressing the test dose as a multiple of the annual outdoor dose for a stated location and mounting.

title: Computational Quantum Chemistry-Based Atmospheric Isotope Fractionation Prediction Framework: Application in Sulfate Aerosol Formation Mechanisms
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Atmospheric isotope serves as an effective source tracer for tracking the pollutants fate. Its precise source apportionment capability is constrained by the comprehensive assessment of isotope fractionation. This study aimed to propose a Computational Quantum Chemistry (CQC)-based Atmospheric Isotope Fractionation Prediction (AIFP) framework. It can quantify the isotope fractionation mechanisms. This framework utilizes CQC to perform a pipeline for reaction mechanism determination, atmospheric species geometry calculation, and parameter post-processing. It integrates the isotope-substitution method with the fractionation model to establish isotope fractionation standard equations in complex atmospheric chemical systems, providing a theoretical basis for atmospheric isotope tracing. This framework was applied to investigate sulfur (34S) fractionation and sulfate (pSO42–) formation. This application developed a localized 34S fractionation parameter scheme, revealing that pSO42– pollution is driven by NO2 and TMI oxidation. These oxidants account for 58.3 ± 1.0% of its pollution, highlighting the critical role of controlling the transformation conditions of key oxidants in haze pollution mitigation. Our framework extends the atmospheric isotope application, providing a rapid and efficient isotope fractionation prediction framework.

title: Small-Molecule Contacts to NMR-Invisible Aβ40 Oligomers Revealed by Pressure-Jump NMR and t 1-Noise Suppression
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Soluble amyloid-β (Aβ) oligomers are widely implicated as neurotoxic species in Alzheimer’s disease but remain difficult to characterize because their transient, heterogeneous assemblies are effectively invisible to conventional solution nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy. Hydrostatic pressure (∼2.2 kbar) dissociates Aβ40 oligomers into monomers with sharp, intense resonances. Here, we exploit this pressure-dependent behavior to detect weak intermolecular contacts formed between small molecules and the NMR-invisible oligomers and read them out after pressure-induced dissociation. Using dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) as a simple small-molecule probe, we combine pressure-jump NMR with NOE difference spectroscopy to obtain residue-resolved DMSO-to-Aβ40-oligomer contacts. Because the resulting NOE signals are very weak, their detection requires substantial suppression of t1 noise that is shown to arise primarily from minute FID-to-FID phase and frequency instabilities. We therefore introduced RePAIR (Reference-based Phase And frequency Instability Reduction), a software package that uses an internal reference resonance to correct per-FID phase and frequency errors in gradient-encoded, phase-modulated data sets, suppressing t1 noise and revealing otherwise hidden intermolecular NOEs. The resulting contact profile shows preferential DMSO interactions with the ordered, hydrophobic β-sheet core of the Aβ40 oligomers. More broadly, this approach provides a framework for obtaining residue-resolved information on weak small-molecule interactions with transient protein assemblies that are otherwise inaccessible to conventional solution NMR.

title: Stereodivergent Synthesis of γ-Functionalized Primary Alcohols via Relay-Synergistic Ir/Amine/Ni Catalysis
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Primary alcohols bearing chiral motifs constitute a class of highly valuable organic compounds that are widely prevalent in natural products and pharmaceutical molecules. Although impressive progress has been made in α- and β-functionalization of primary alcohols, the development of efficient methods for the synthesis of the γ-functionalized primary alcohols─particularly in an asymmetric fashion─remains a significant challenge. Here we report a relay-synergistic Ir/amine/Ni catalytic manifold that converts primary allylic alcohols into γ-functionalized primary alcohols bearing adjacent γ,δ-stereocenters with full catalyst-controlled stereodivergence. The reaction proceeds sequentially through iridium-catalyzed borrowing hydrogen to oxidize the primary allylic alcohol, followed by a stereodetermining Michael addition cooperatively catalyzed by a chiral amine and a chiral nickel catalyst, and concludes with iridium-hydride-mediated reduction. A series of primary alcohols bearing adjacent γ,δ-stereocenters could be easily synthesized in moderate to excellent yields and with good to excellent stereoselectivities (up to 94% yield, >20:1 dr, >99% ee). By permuting the configurations of the amine and nickel catalysts, all four stereoisomers can be accessed. Remarkably, control experiments indicate that the relay-synergistic strategy suppresses retro-Michael addition by rapidly reducing the unstable Michael adduct, thereby maintaining high diastereoselectivity. Kinetic isotope experiments identify the borrowing-hydrogen oxidation of the primary allylic alcohol as the rate-determining step.

title: Gas–Water Interfacial Conversion of CO2-Derived Carbamates to Substituted Ureas
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Amines (RNH2) capture carbon dioxide (CO2) in water as carbamates (RNHCO2–), one C–N bond short of a urea (RNHCONHR′). Interfacial studies have so far produced only unsubstituted urea from inorganic nitrogen sources, whereas conversion of organic carbamates to substituted ureas at aqueous interfaces remains unexamined. Here we show that gas–water interfaces (GWIs) promote this downstream step under ambient aqueous conditions. When an aqueous solution of amines is pneumatically nebulized with CO2, some of the initially formed carbamates convert to substituted ureas, including cyclic products from diamines and intermolecular products from monoamines. 13CO2 labeling traces the urea carbonyl carbon to CO2, and offline chromatographic comparison against an authentic standard further identifies the product independent of the online mass spectrometry. Pure CO2 nebulization gives the strongest urea signals, and longer droplet flight times increase the apparent urea ion fraction. Structurally matched substrates and crossed-spray experiments link dehydration to ring-closure geometry, steric/electronic structure, and amine nucleophilicity. Density functional theory and exploratory ab initio metadynamics support a proton-assisted ionic dehydration pathway modulated by interfacial electric fields and water-mediated proton transfer. These results identify GWIs as reactive microenvironments that drive aqueous CO2–amine chemistry toward carbamate-to-urea conversion without added coupling reagents.

title: Tumor-Specific Gene Editing Enhances Cancer Immunogenicity through Succinate Metabolism-Mediated MHC-I Reprogramming
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Impaired expression of major histocompatibility complex class I (MHC-I) greatly compromises cytotoxic T-cell-mediated anticancer immunotherapy. Existing MHC-I activation strategies are greatly challenged by poor tumor specificity and off-target toxicity. Herein, we report a dual tumor-specific CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing system that can precisely knock out succinate dehydrogenase subunit C (Sdhc) to activate the MHC-I pathway via epigenetic and transcriptional regulation. A tumor-specific gene editor is first engineered via reversible shielding of sgRNA using an apurinic/apyrimidinic endonuclease 1 (APE1)-responsive, complementary ssDNA, yielding AP-sgRNA with blocked editing activity in normal cells yet completely restored activity in APE1-overexpressing tumor cells. Subsequently, tumor-targeted delivery of AP-sgRNA and Cas9 mRNA (mCas9) is achieved using dibenzocyclooctyne-decorated lipid nanoparticle (DLNP), which upon bioorthogonal click reaction can anchor cancer cells that are prelabeled with azido groups using the unnatural sugar DCL-AAM. Thus, AP-sgSdhc/mCas9@DLNP enables efficient and selective Sdhc editing in tumor cells, leading to epigenetic and transcriptional activation of MHC-antigen processing and presentation genes and thereby provoking robust antitumor efficacy in the B16-OVA melanoma model through enhanced, T cell-mediated immune responses. Moreover, it completely suppressed pulmonary metastasis after combination with aPD-L1 in the 4T1 lung metastasis model. This study provides an enlightened paradigm for precision gene editing and renders a promising mechanism for potentiating cancer immunotherapy.

title: Guest-Programmed Adaptive Redistribution in Heteroleptic Metal–Organic Cages
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Adaptive reconfiguration of complex supramolecular assemblies remains a fundamental challenge in synthetic chemistry, especially for heteroleptic systems prone to kinetic traps and component scrambling. Here, we report a guest-coupled reassembly strategy that enables programmable redistribution between cage architectures in heteroleptic pentagonal prismatic ZnII cages, assembled via precise edge-length matching between pentatopic and tetratopic ligands. Distinct from conventional single-guest templation, these cages exhibit adaptive redistribution behavior in which multiguest recognition is coupled to host redistribution within confined cavities. Chlorinated guests are selectively encapsulated through Cl···π and π···π interactions, thereby biasing the thermodynamic landscape of assembly. Secondary guests redirect the assembly equilibrium toward distinct product distributions, including guest release, guest exchange, or stoichiometry-dependent formation of species assigned as a homoleptic pseudo-cubic cage with one or two encapsulated guests. Crystallographic, Hirshfeld surface, and computational analyses reveal that multiple Cl···π, π···π, and C–H···π noncovalent interactions within the confined cavity contribute to the selectivity of guest-directed assembly redistribution. Furthermore, the incorporation of peripheral pyrene units imparts the prismatic cages with photoluminescence, which is enhanced upon guest binding due to framework rigidification. This work demonstrates how confined multiguest recognition can be coupled to compositional redistribution within complex heteroleptic assemblies, providing a foundation for programmable adaptive supramolecular systems.

title: Tellurium–Oxygen Molecules Bridging MFI Zeolite Nanoplates into a b -Oriented Membrane for CO2 Separation
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract The orientation of zeolite pores parallel to gas transport can facilitate rapid selective gas separation; however, the fabrication of oriented zeolite membranes remains a grand challenge. This study reports a unique strategy of molecularly bridging zeolite nanoplates to fabricate a b-oriented MFI membrane for CO2 gas separation. Tellurium alkoxide of Te(C3H6O2)2 is designed as the bridging agent, and the MFI zeolite nanoplate is synthesized in the aspect ratio of ∼14 as the building block. The bridging of MFI nanoplates occurs via the condensation reaction with tellurium alkoxide, and the resultant membrane exhibits b-orientation with straight pores of ∼ 5 Å running perpendicular to the membrane surface. The molecular bridging enables high membrane continuity for CO2 separation with exceptional separation factors of 33.0 and 36.8 for CO2/N2 and CO2/CH4, respectively. The straight pores bestow high CO2 permeance up to 20 × 10–7 mol m–2 s–1 Pa–1. This strategy is advantageous over conventional approaches by virtue of better control on membrane orientation and less dependence on support. The superior performance compared to those of the state-of-the-art zeolite membranes promises such b-oriented MFI membranes great potential in industrial CO2 separation.

title: Embracing Phase Transitions to Rationalize the High Oxygen Evolution Reaction Activity of Nickel Selenides in Alkaline Electrolytes
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract The transformation of electrodeposited NiSe nanocatalysts was studied under oxygen evolution reaction (OER) conditions in alkaline electrolytes by a combination of operando X-ray absorption (XAS) and operando electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS). The upper layers of nickel selenides transform into nickel oxide/oxyhydroxide species, which exhibit higher catalytic OER activity than the as-synthesized nickel oxide/oxyhydroxide, as reported previously. The coupled operando XAS and EIS experiments reveal that the Ni3+/Ni4+ transition occurs at lower potentials than the OER, involving a transient phase transformation at the foot of the nickel oxidation peak.
